description_raw: A World-Changing Company Palantir builds the world’s leading software for data-driven decisions and operations. By bringing the right data to the people who need it, our platforms empower our partners to develop lifesaving drugs, forecast supply chain disruptions, locate missing children, and more. The Role The Connectivity team builds the software that connects Palantir’s platform to customer systems. Our connectors integrate databases, enterprise applications, cloud storage, web services, and streaming systems, enabling customers to bring data into Foundry and write back to their operational systems. From large datasets to real-time events and user-driven interactions, these connections underpin the applications and AI workflows customers build with Foundry and AIP. You’ll build and maintain Foundry’s first-class connector suite and the shared infrastructure behind it. You’ll work across the stack, taking ownership of connector implementations, developer SDKs, and the systems that build, test, distribute, and run our connectivity software. A central part of this work is evolving and scaling a large, established codebase. You’ll move integrations from bespoke infrastructure onto shared platform capabilities, design SDKs that enable other teams and customers to build integrations independently, and safely retire older implementations. You’ll also build observability and diagnostic tools that help users understand, monitor, and troubleshoot their connections. You’ll own improvements from design through production and use what you learn from operating connectors to strengthen the platform they share. Salary The estimated salary range for this position is estimated to be $135,000 - $200,000/year. Total compensation for this position may also include Restricted Stock units, sign-on bonus and other potential future incentives. Further note that total compensation for this position will be determined by each individual’s relevant qualifications, work experience, skills, and other factors. This estimate excludes the value of any potential sign-on bonus; the value of any benefits offered; and the potential future value of any long-term incentives. Life at Palantir We want every Palantirian to achieve their best outcomes, that’s why we celebrate individuals’ strengths, skills, and interests, from your first interview to your longterm growth, rather than rely on traditional career ladders. Paying attention to the needs of our community enables us to optimize our opportunities to grow and helps ensure many pathways to success at Palantir. Promoting health and well-being across all areas of Palantirians’ lives is just one of the ways we’re investing in our community. Learn more at Life at Palantir and note that our offerings may vary by region. In keeping consistent with Palantir’s values and culture, we believe employees are “better together” and in-person work affords the opportunity for more creative outcomes. Therefore, we encourage employees to work from our offices to foster connectivity and innovation. Many teams do offer hybrid options (WFH a day or two a week), allowing our employees to strike the right trade-off for their personal productivity. Based on business need, there are a few roles that allow for “Remote” work on an exceptional basis. If you are applying for one of these roles, you must work from the city and or country in which you are employed. If the posting is specified as Onsite, you are required to work from an office. If you want to empower the world's most important institutions, you belong here. Palantir values excellence regardless of background. We are committed to making the application and hiring process accessible to everyone and will provide a reasonable accommodation for those living with a disability. If you need an accommodation for the application or hiring process , please reach out and let us know how we can help. Please note that you will never be asked to submit a payment or share financial information to participate in our interview process. If you suspect that you've been contacted by a scammer, we recommend you cease all communication with the individual and consider reporting them to the relevant authorities, such as the US FBI Internet Crime Complaint Center (IC3) .

lists.content:
• Java and Python for connectors, backend services, and developer SDKs
  • Open-source technologies like Kafka, Kubernetes, Flink, Debezium, Iceberg
  • Industry-standard build tooling, including Gradle and GitHub
  • Shared job orchestration, streaming, serverless execution, and compute deployment platforms

• Build and maintain Foundry’s first-class connectors, improving performance and extending support for imports, exports, change data capture, interactive queries, and writeback as external systems and customer needs evolve.
  • Improve the infrastructure that builds, tests, packages, and distributes connectors and shared libraries, including tooling across our connector monorepo.
  • Design and maintain connectivity SDKs for internal teams and end users, with clear APIs, documentation, testing utilities, and development workflows that make integrations easy to author and maintain.
  • Collaborate with product teams to integrate connector execution with job orchestration, streaming, and serverless platforms.
  • Lead incremental migrations onto shared infrastructure, manage compatibility, and retire older implementations while preserving the workflows customers depend on.
  • Develop reusable security frameworks and tooling that make secure connectivity a consistent part of connector development and execution.
  • Debug production issues and performance problems across the stack, turning recurring support problems into durable fixes, automated tests, and better observability.
  • Establish shared testing frameworks, compatibility checks, and release practices that keep a large connector portfolio reliable and maintainable.
  • Help prepare and maintain Palantir connectivity software for open-source use, including its APIs, packaging, documentation, and contributor experience.

• An ownership mindset and a high bar for correctness, security, and automated testing, including responsibility for how software behaves in production.
  • Pride in building and maintaining integrations over time, including the detailed work required to keep them reliable as upstream systems change.
  • Engineering judgment that balances delivering new capabilities with simplifying existing systems and reducing operational burden.
  • Empathy for developers and end users, reflected in usable SDKs, clear configuration, actionable errors, and useful diagnostics.
  • Curiosity about unfamiliar systems and persistence in debugging problems across languages, APIs, services, networks, and execution environments.

• 4+ years of professional software engineering experience developing external system connectors, with depth in areas such as developing batch and streaming data ingestion systems, third-party integration development, or monorepo and asset distribution frameworks. Operating on top of these technologies alone does not qualify.
  • Deep expertise in Gradle, including developing custom plugins, managing multi-project builds, and optimizing build performance.
  • Demonstrated ability to diagnose complex reliability and performance problems and improve systems through measured, incremental changes.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills and the ability to work effectively across teams, incorporate feedback, and hold a high bar for quality.

As a Platform Engineer on Palantir's Identity Platform team, you will design, build, and operate secure-by-design identity infrastructure and tooling. Your goal will be to make the secure path the easy path. Your work will directly strengthen the identity substrate beneath Palantir's most critical deployments, from a globally distributed workforce to regulated and air-gapped environments.

lists.content:
• Develop automation and tooling for corporate and customer-facing identity platforms
  • Build, secure, and manage geo-redundant containerized services (EKS and ECS) in AWS and Azure
  • Scale the implementation of Single Sign-On (SSO) integrations across multiple Entra ID tenants using infrastructure-as-code frameworks
  • Build tooling to standardize and scale operational workflows across AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud Platform (GCP)
  • Extend the identity platform to non-human identities, treating workloads and AI agents as first-class principals with scoped, short-lived credentials
  • Build the governance layer: an access graph that makes entitlements legible and a policy engine that makes authorization decisions enforceable and auditable
  • Design token-issuance and federation flows that make least-privilege, ephemeral access the default
  • Research and drive adoption of emerging authentication and session security standards (such as device-bound session credentials and continuous access evaluation) in collaboration with Security Engineers
  • Pressure-test designs and partner with Identity Security Engineers to threat model implementations before they ship
  • Partner with Security Compliance Engineers to build services that reduce the cost and complexity of compliance enforcement

• Technical proficiency in identity protocols (SAML, OIDC, OAuth 2.0, LDAP, Kerberos, FIDO2, WebAuthn)
  • Experience managing identities and governance workflows on platforms such as Entra ID, Keycloak, AWS Cognito, or Okta
  • Experience with policy engines and authorization-as-code, and with relationship-based access modeling or entitlement graph design
  • Experience with token issuance and federation, including OAuth 2.0 token exchange, short-lived credentials, and workload identity federation
  • Non-human identity experience: workload and machine identity (service-to-service authentication, mTLS, workload attestation), plus interest in agentic identity (agents as principals, delegation and on-behalf-of flows, and attribution across a delegation chain)

• 3+ years of experience in Site Reliability Engineering (SRE), DevOps, software engineering, or an equivalent discipline, with a strong passion for security
  • Experience deploying and operating containerized services (EKS, ECS, or similar) in AWS, Azure, or Google Cloud
  • Experience building and operating production services or APIs, not only automation scripts
  • Expert-level proficiency in a language such as Go (preferred), Python, or TypeScript
  • Experience with infrastructure-as-code (Terraform, Helm, CloudFormation, or similar)
  • An active TS/SCI security clearance, or eligibility and willingness to obtain one

The Role

As a Platform Engineer on Palantir's Identity Platform team, you will design, build, and operate secure-by-design identity infrastructure and tooling. You will make identity governance and access management easier and more secure to implement for Palantirians and customers worldwide. As part of Palantir's best-in-class Information Security organization, you will research, implement, and scale innovative solutions that help Palantir stay ahead of a dynamic threat landscape.

You will help the team build the next-generation identity platform that treats agents and workload identities as first-class principals: the access graph that makes entitlements legible, the policy engine that makes authorization enforceable and auditable, and the token-issuance layer that keeps access short-lived, scoped, and least-privilege by default. Your work will shape the arc of these components from design to production.

You will join the high-performing Identity Platform team, engineers who are passionate about delivering identity outcomes at scale that reduce risk and friction. The team builds and operates the identity platforms that serve both corporate and production (customer-facing) infrastructure, and the paved-road tooling and secure baselines that teams across Palantir deploy on. Your goal will be to make the secure path the easy path. Your work will directly strengthen the identity substrate beneath Palantir's most critical deployments, from a globally distributed workforce to regulated and air-gapped environments.

lists.content:
• Develop automation and tooling for corporate and customer-facing identity platforms
  • Build, secure, and manage geo-redundant containerized services (EKS and ECS) in AWS and Azure
  • Scale the implementation of Single Sign-On (SSO) integrations across multiple Entra ID tenants using infrastructure-as-code frameworks
  • Build tooling to standardize and scale operational workflows across AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud Platform (GCP)
  • Extend the identity platform to non-human identities, treating workloads and AI agents as first-class principals with scoped, short-lived credentials
  • Build the governance layer: an access graph that makes entitlements legible and a policy engine that makes authorization decisions enforceable and auditable
  • Design token-issuance and federation flows that make least-privilege, ephemeral access the default
  • Research and drive adoption of emerging authentication and session security standards (such as device-bound session credentials and continuous access evaluation) in collaboration with Security Engineers
  • Pressure-test designs and partner with Identity Security Engineers to threat model implementations before they ship
  • Partner with Security Compliance Engineers to build services that reduce the cost and complexity of compliance enforcement

• Technical proficiency in identity protocols (SAML, OIDC, OAuth 2.0, LDAP, Kerberos, FIDO2, WebAuthn)
  • Experience managing identities and governance workflows on platforms such as Entra ID, Keycloak, AWS Cognito, or Okta
  • Experience with policy engines and authorization-as-code, and with relationship-based access modeling or entitlement graph design
  • Experience with token issuance and federation, including OAuth 2.0 token exchange, short-lived credentials, and workload identity federation
  • Non-human identity experience: workload and machine identity (service-to-service authentication, mTLS, workload attestation), plus interest in agentic identity (agents as principals, delegation and on-behalf-of flows, and attribution across a delegation chain)

• 3+ years of experience in Site Reliability Engineering (SRE), DevOps, software engineering, or an equivalent discipline, with a strong passion for security
  • Experience deploying and operating containerized services (EKS, ECS, or similar) in AWS, Azure, or Google Cloud
  • Experience building and operating production services or APIs, not only automation scripts
  • Expert-level proficiency in a language such as Go (preferred), Python, or TypeScript
  • Experience with infrastructure-as-code (Terraform, Helm, CloudFormation, or similar)
  • An active TS/SCI security clearance, or eligibility and willingness to obtain one

As a Software Engineer, you'll collaborate closely with technical and non-technical counterparts to understand our customers' problems and build products that solve them.
 
Please note that this posting is open to all levels of experience.

raw_payload.descriptionPlain:
A World-Changing Company
 
Palantir builds the world’s leading software for data-driven decisions and operations. By bringing the right data to the people who need it, our platforms empower our partners to develop lifesaving drugs, forecast supply chain disruptions, locate missing children, and more.


The Role
 
If you joined us today, you get to author the strategy by which each of Palantir’s software platforms - Foundry, Gotham, Apollo - achieves full containerization across an intimidating diversity of infrastructure types. Tomorrow, you get to do the same for Palantir’s ever expanding customer community. You will drive those goals by building elegant, robust APIs powered by K8s controllers which bridge the gap between a raw Kubernetes cluster and a fully-featured, infrastructure agnostic runtime that can scale to the operational needs of 100s of specialized microservices. Joining you on that journey is a highly motivated team with a diverse group of backgrounds and skillsets, brimming with ambition.

lists.content:
• Engage with and internalize Palantir’s infrastructure strategy and the needs of your team’s customer base.
  • Deeply understand and leverage K8s primitives, the broader OSS ecosystem around K8s, and highly technical service lifecycle semantics to solve business critical problems at scale.
  • Build and evolve the APIs through which in-house as well as third-party software developers interact with K8s to satisfy their runtime needs, cleanly abstracting away the complex distributed systems powering them.
  • Work closely with your team and stakeholders to enable sustainable and timely delivery of technical solutions to address business needs.
  • Champion a long-term tech roadmap to reduce operational burden, ensure scalability, reduce risk, and strive for step-changes whenever possible.

• Clear and concise verbal and written communications.
  • A focus on impact and an ability to articulate the value your work provides.
  • Experience developing and managing highly-available distributed systems.
  • Passion for designing thoughtful and robust APIs.
  • Deep familiarity with K8s, and the broader ecosystem of software around K8s.

• 3+ years of professional software development experience.
  • 1+ years of experience contributing to the system design or architecture (architecture, design patterns, reliability and scaling) of new and existing systems.
  • 1+years of experience as a mentor, tech lead or leading an engineering team.
  • Strong coding skills in Go, Java, or equivalent.
  • Experience designing, building, and operating high-scale observability or infrastructure systems.
  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science or equivalent.

title_raw: Software Engineer, Intern - Connectivity Platform and Product
description_raw: A World-Changing Company Palantir builds the world’s leading software for data-driven decisions and operations. By bringing the right data to the people who need it, our platforms empower our partners to develop lifesaving drugs, forecast supply chain disruptions, locate missing children, and more. The Role The Connectivity team builds products that connect our most critical institutions to their most critical data. Our products securely integrate databases, enterprise applications, cloud storage, web services, and streaming systems, enabling customers to bring data into Foundry and write back to their operational systems. raw_payload.descriptionPlain:
A World-Changing Company
 
Palantir builds the world’s leading software for data-driven decisions and operations. By bringing the right data to the people who need it, our platforms empower our partners to develop lifesaving drugs, forecast supply chain disruptions, locate missing children, and more.


The Role
 
The Connectivity team builds products that connect our most critical institutions to their most critical data. Our products securely integrate databases, enterprise applications, cloud storage, web services, and streaming systems, enabling customers to bring data into Foundry and write back to their operational systems. We build applications, frameworks, and infrastructure for connectivity across Foundry: high scale data processing pipelines, user-written code, AI agents, or connecting directly from the Ontology.

You’ll work across the stack, owning and building out features across our UI, backend services, and compute platforms. You’ll iterate closely with experienced engineers, FDEs, and other teams to scope and build out new Connectivity products and integrations, as well as building toolkits to support those integrations: APIs, SDKs, authentication flows, security frameworks, and changes to core products across the platform. The work is highly technical, collaborative, dynamic, and follows customer signal closely.

This role is expected to be about 75% backend and 25% frontend.
 

Core Responsibilities
 
We're hiring high agency engineers who are passionate about solving real-world problems. If you’re motivated to enable outcomes with connectivity, here are some examples of the types of work you’d get to do:
Build SDKs and integrations that allow customers and internal product teams to write code to connect to external systemsLaunch features to enable entirely new paradigms of data connectionDive deep into Foundry security and the bleeding edge of securing connected AI agents and pipelines in sensitive environmentsIdentify, diagnose, and remediate performance and correctness issues for high scale connectivity workflowsWork with infrastructure teams to expose powerful networking functionality to usersCraft elegant workflows to enable customers to maximally leverage their data systemsScale nascent connectivity products from first use to billionsLearn and build across a large suite of repos, services, and domains

Technologies We Use
Java and PythonOpen-source technologies like Cassandra, Kubernetes, Envoy, GraphQL, and ReactProtocols such as TCP, UDP, TLS, HTTPGradle for builds and GitHub for collaborationShared job orchestration, streaming, serverless execution, and compute deployment platforms
You do not need prior experience with these technologies. We expect you to learn them here.

    • Identify, diagnose, and remediate performance and correctness issues for high scale connectivity workflows

lists.content:
• Curiosity about connectivity in cloud systems, from networking to productization to security and authentication
  • An ownership mindset and a high bar for usability, security, and correctness, including responsibility for how software behaves in production.
  • Comfort following problems across languages, APIs, services, networks, and execution environments
  • Eagerness to learn, ask questions, and incorporate feedback

• Currently pursuing or recently completed a Bachelor's, Master's, or PhD in Computer Science, Mathematics, Software Engineering, Physics, or a similar field, or equivalent practical experience
  • Proficiency in at least one language such as Java, Python, TypeScript, or Go
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills
  • Coursework, projects, or practical experience in one or more of computer networks, distributed systems, databases, cloud computing, or software architecture.
  • Must be planning on graduating in 2028. This should be your final internship before graduating.

description_raw: A World-Changing Company Palantir builds the world’s leading software for data-driven decisions and operations. By bringing the right data to the people who need it, our platforms empower our partners to develop lifesaving drugs, forecast supply chain disruptions, locate missing children, and more. The Role The Connectivity team builds the software that connects Palantir’s platform to customer systems. Our connectors integrate databases, enterprise applications, cloud storage, web services, and streaming systems, enabling customers to bring data into Foundry and write back to their operational systems. From large datasets to real-time events and user-driven interactions, these connections underpin the applications and AI workflows customers build with Foundry and AIP. You’ll build and maintain Foundry’s first-class connector suite and the shared infrastructure behind it. You’ll work across the stack, taking ownership of connector implementations, developer SDKs, and the systems that build, test, distribute, and run our connectivity software. A central part of this work is evolving and scaling a large, established codebase. You’ll move integrations from bespoke infrastructure onto shared platform capabilities, design SDKs that enable other teams and customers to build integrations independently, and safely retire older implementations. You’ll also build observability and diagnostic tools that help users understand, monitor, and troubleshoot their connections. You’ll own improvements from design through production and use what you learn from operating connectors to strengthen the platform they share. Salary The estimated salary range for this position is estimated to be $135,000 - $200,000/year. Total compensation for this position may also include Restricted Stock units, sign-on bonus and other potential future incentives. Further note that total compensation for this position will be determined by each individual’s relevant qualifications, work experience, skills, and other factors. This estimate excludes the value of any potential sign-on bonus; the value of any benefits offered; and the potential future value of any long-term incentives. Life at Palantir We want every Palantirian to achieve their best outcomes, that’s why we celebrate individuals’ strengths, skills, and interests, from your first interview to your longterm growth, rather than rely on traditional career ladders. Paying attention to the needs of our community enables us to optimize our opportunities to grow and helps ensure many pathways to success at Palantir. Promoting health and well-being across all areas of Palantirians’ lives is just one of the ways we’re investing in our community. Learn more at Life at Palantir and note that our offerings may vary by region. In keeping consistent with Palantir’s values and culture, we believe employees are “better together” and in-person work affords the opportunity for more creative outcomes. Therefore, we encourage employees to work from our offices to foster connectivity and innovation. Many teams do offer hybrid options (WFH a day or two a week), allowing our employees to strike the right trade-off for their personal productivity. Based on business need, there are a few roles that allow for “Remote” work on an exceptional basis. If you are applying for one of these roles, you must work from the city and or country in which you are employed. If the posting is specified as Onsite, you are required to work from an office. If you want to empower the world's most important institutions, you belong here. Palantir values excellence regardless of background. We are committed to making the application and hiring process accessible to everyone and will provide a reasonable accommodation for those living with a disability. If you need an accommodation for the application or hiring process , please reach out and let us know how we can help. Please note that you will never be asked to submit a payment or share financial information to participate in our interview process. If you suspect that you've been contacted by a scammer, we recommend you cease all communication with the individual and consider reporting them to the relevant authorities, such as the US FBI Internet Crime Complaint Center (IC3) .

lists.content:
• Java and Python for connectors, backend services, and developer SDKs
  • Open-source technologies like Kafka, Kubernetes, Flink, Debezium, Iceberg
  • Industry-standard build tooling, including Gradle and GitHub
  • Shared job orchestration, streaming, serverless execution, and compute deployment platforms

• Build and maintain Foundry’s first-class connectors, improving performance and extending support for imports, exports, change data capture, interactive queries, and writeback as external systems and customer needs evolve.
  • Improve the infrastructure that builds, tests, packages, and distributes connectors and shared libraries, including tooling across our connector monorepo.
  • Design and maintain connectivity SDKs for internal teams and end users, with clear APIs, documentation, testing utilities, and development workflows that make integrations easy to author and maintain.
  • Collaborate with product teams to integrate connector execution with job orchestration, streaming, and serverless platforms.
  • Lead incremental migrations onto shared infrastructure, manage compatibility, and retire older implementations while preserving the workflows customers depend on.
  • Develop reusable security frameworks and tooling that make secure connectivity a consistent part of connector development and execution.
  • Debug production issues and performance problems across the stack, turning recurring support problems into durable fixes, automated tests, and better observability.
  • Establish shared testing frameworks, compatibility checks, and release practices that keep a large connector portfolio reliable and maintainable.
  • Help prepare and maintain Palantir connectivity software for open-source use, including its APIs, packaging, documentation, and contributor experience.

• An ownership mindset and a high bar for correctness, security, and automated testing, including responsibility for how software behaves in production.
  • Pride in building and maintaining integrations over time, including the detailed work required to keep them reliable as upstream systems change.
  • Engineering judgment that balances delivering new capabilities with simplifying existing systems and reducing operational burden.
  • Empathy for developers and end users, reflected in usable SDKs, clear configuration, actionable errors, and useful diagnostics.
  • Curiosity about unfamiliar systems and persistence in debugging problems across languages, APIs, services, networks, and execution environments.

• 4+ years of professional software engineering experience developing external system connectors, with depth in areas such as developing batch and streaming data ingestion systems, third-party integration development, or monorepo and asset distribution frameworks. Operating on top of these technologies alone does not qualify.
  • Deep expertise in Gradle, including developing custom plugins, managing multi-project builds, and optimizing build performance.
  • Demonstrated ability to diagnose complex reliability and performance problems and improve systems through measured, incremental changes.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills and the ability to work effectively across teams, incorporate feedback, and hold a high bar for quality.

A World-Changing Company
 
Palantir builds the world’s leading software for data-driven decisions and operations. By bringing the right data to the people who need it, our platforms empower our partners to develop lifesaving drugs, forecast supply chain disruptions, locate missing children, and more.


The Role
As a Platform Engineer on Palantir's Identity Platform team, you will design, build, and operate secure-by-design identity infrastructure and tooling. You will make identity governance and access management easier and more secure to implement for Palantirians and customers worldwide. As part of Palantir's best-in-class Information Security organization, you will research, implement, and scale innovative solutions that help Palantir stay ahead of a dynamic threat landscape.

You will help the team build the next-generation identity platform that treats agents and workload identities as first-class principals: the access graph that makes entitlements legible, the policy engine that makes authorization enforceable and auditable, and the token-issuance layer that keeps access short-lived, scoped, and least-privilege by default. Your work will shape the arc of these components from design to production.

You will join the high-performing Identity Platform team, engineers who are passionate about delivering identity outcomes at scale that reduce risk and friction. The team builds and operates the identity platforms that serve both corporate and production (customer-facing) infrastructure, and the paved-road tooling and secure baselines that teams across Palantir deploy on. Your goal will be to make the secure path the easy path. Your work will directly strengthen the identity substrate beneath Palantir's most critical deployments, from a globally distributed workforce to regulated and air-gapped environments.

lists.content:
• Develop automation and tooling for corporate and customer-facing identity platforms
  • Build, secure, and manage geo-redundant containerized services (EKS and ECS) in AWS and Azure
  • Scale the implementation of Single Sign-On (SSO) integrations across multiple Entra ID tenants using infrastructure-as-code frameworks
  • Build tooling to standardize and scale operational workflows across AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud Platform (GCP)
  • Extend the identity platform to non-human identities, treating workloads and AI agents as first-class principals with scoped, short-lived credentials
  • Build the governance layer: an access graph that makes entitlements legible and a policy engine that makes authorization decisions enforceable and auditable
  • Design token-issuance and federation flows that make least-privilege, ephemeral access the default
  • Research and drive adoption of emerging authentication and session security standards (such as device-bound session credentials and continuous access evaluation) in collaboration with Security Engineers
  • Pressure-test designs and partner with Identity Security Engineers to threat model implementations before they ship
  • Partner with Security Compliance Engineers to build services that reduce the cost and complexity of compliance enforcement

• Technical proficiency in identity protocols (SAML, OIDC, OAuth 2.0, LDAP, Kerberos, FIDO2, WebAuthn)
  • Experience managing identities and governance workflows on platforms such as Entra ID, Keycloak, AWS Cognito, or Okta
  • Experience with policy engines and authorization-as-code, and with relationship-based access modeling or entitlement graph design
  • Experience with token issuance and federation, including OAuth 2.0 token exchange, short-lived credentials, and workload identity federation
  • Non-human identity experience: workload and machine identity (service-to-service authentication, mTLS, workload attestation), plus interest in agentic identity (agents as principals, delegation and on-behalf-of flows, and attribution across a delegation chain)

• 3+ years of experience in Site Reliability Engineering (SRE), DevOps, software engineering, or an equivalent discipline, with a strong passion for security
  • Experience deploying and operating containerized services (EKS, ECS, or similar) in AWS, Azure, or Google Cloud
  • Experience building and operating production services or APIs, not only automation scripts
  • Expert-level proficiency in a language such as Go (preferred), Python, or TypeScript
  • Experience with infrastructure-as-code (Terraform, Helm, CloudFormation, or similar)
  • An active TS/SCI security clearance, or eligibility and willingness to obtain one

raw_payload.description:
A World-Changing Company
 
Palantir builds the world’s leading software for data-driven decisions and operations. By bringing the right data to the people who need it, our platforms empower our partners to develop lifesaving drugs, forecast supply chain disruptions, locate missing children, and more.

The Role

As a Platform Engineer on Palantir's Identity Platform team, you will design, build, and operate secure-by-design identity infrastructure and tooling. You will make identity governance and access management easier and more secure to implement for Palantirians and customers worldwide. As part of Palantir's best-in-class Information Security organization, you will research, implement, and scale innovative solutions that help Palantir stay ahead of a dynamic threat landscape.

You will help the team build the next-generation identity platform that treats agents and workload identities as first-class principals: the access graph that makes entitlements legible, the policy engine that makes authorization enforceable and auditable, and the token-issuance layer that keeps access short-lived, scoped, and least-privilege by default. Your work will shape the arc of these components from design to production.

You will join the high-performing Identity Platform team, engineers who are passionate about delivering identity outcomes at scale that reduce risk and friction. The team builds and operates the identity platforms that serve both corporate and production (customer-facing) infrastructure, and the paved-road tooling and secure baselines that teams across Palantir deploy on. Your goal will be to make the secure path the easy path. Your work will directly strengthen the identity substrate beneath Palantir's most critical deployments, from a globally distributed workforce to regulated and air-gapped environments.

lists.content:
• Develop automation and tooling for corporate and customer-facing identity platforms
  • Build, secure, and manage geo-redundant containerized services (EKS and ECS) in AWS and Azure
  • Scale the implementation of Single Sign-On (SSO) integrations across multiple Entra ID tenants using infrastructure-as-code frameworks
  • Build tooling to standardize and scale operational workflows across AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud Platform (GCP)
  • Extend the identity platform to non-human identities, treating workloads and AI agents as first-class principals with scoped, short-lived credentials
  • Build the governance layer: an access graph that makes entitlements legible and a policy engine that makes authorization decisions enforceable and auditable
  • Design token-issuance and federation flows that make least-privilege, ephemeral access the default
  • Research and drive adoption of emerging authentication and session security standards (such as device-bound session credentials and continuous access evaluation) in collaboration with Security Engineers
  • Pressure-test designs and partner with Identity Security Engineers to threat model implementations before they ship
  • Partner with Security Compliance Engineers to build services that reduce the cost and complexity of compliance enforcement

• Technical proficiency in identity protocols (SAML, OIDC, OAuth 2.0, LDAP, Kerberos, FIDO2, WebAuthn)
  • Experience managing identities and governance workflows on platforms such as Entra ID, Keycloak, AWS Cognito, or Okta
  • Experience with policy engines and authorization-as-code, and with relationship-based access modeling or entitlement graph design
  • Experience with token issuance and federation, including OAuth 2.0 token exchange, short-lived credentials, and workload identity federation
  • Non-human identity experience: workload and machine identity (service-to-service authentication, mTLS, workload attestation), plus interest in agentic identity (agents as principals, delegation and on-behalf-of flows, and attribution across a delegation chain)

• 3+ years of experience in Site Reliability Engineering (SRE), DevOps, software engineering, or an equivalent discipline, with a strong passion for security
  • Experience deploying and operating containerized services (EKS, ECS, or similar) in AWS, Azure, or Google Cloud
  • Experience building and operating production services or APIs, not only automation scripts
  • Expert-level proficiency in a language such as Go (preferred), Python, or TypeScript
  • Experience with infrastructure-as-code (Terraform, Helm, CloudFormation, or similar)
  • An active TS/SCI security clearance, or eligibility and willingness to obtain one

A World-Changing Company
 
Palantir builds the world’s leading software for data-driven decisions and operations. By bringing the right data to the people who need it, our platforms empower our partners to develop lifesaving drugs, forecast supply chain disruptions, locate missing children, and more.


The Role
 
If you joined us today, you get to author the strategy by which each of Palantir’s software platforms - Foundry, Gotham, Apollo - achieves full containerization across an intimidating diversity of infrastructure types. Tomorrow, you get to do the same for Palantir’s ever expanding customer community. You will drive those goals by building elegant, robust APIs powered by K8s controllers which bridge the gap between a raw Kubernetes cluster and a fully-featured, infrastructure agnostic runtime that can scale to the operational needs of 100s of specialized microservices. Joining you on that journey is a highly motivated team with a diverse group of backgrounds and skillsets, brimming with ambition.

lists.content:

• 3+ years of professional software development experience.

  • Strong coding skills in Go, Java, or equivalent.
  • Experience designing, building, and operating high-scale observability or infrastructure systems.
  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science or equivalent.

title_raw: Software Engineer, Intern - Connectivity Platform and Product
description_raw: A World-Changing Company Palantir builds the world’s leading software for data-driven decisions and operations. By bringing the right data to the people who need it, our platforms empower our partners to develop lifesaving drugs, forecast supply chain disruptions, locate missing children, and more. The Role The Connectivity team builds products that connect our most critical institutions to their most critical data. Our products securely integrate databases, enterprise applications, cloud storage, web services, and streaming systems, enabling customers to bring data into Foundry and write back to their operational systems. We build applications, frameworks, and infrastructure for connectivity across Foundry: high scale data processing pipelines, user-written code, AI agents, or connecting directly from the Ontology. You’ll work across the stack, owning and building out features across our UI, backend services, and compute platforms. You’ll iterate closely with experienced engineers, FDEs, and other teams to scope and build out new Connectivity products and integrations, as well as building toolkits to support those integrations: APIs, SDKs, authentication flows, security frameworks, and changes to core products across the platform. The work is highly technical, collaborative, dynamic, and follows customer signal closely. This role is expected to be about 75% backend and 25% frontend. Core Responsibilities We're hiring high agency engineers who are passionate about solving real-world problems. raw_payload.descriptionPlain:
A World-Changing Company
 
Palantir builds the world’s leading software for data-driven decisions and operations. By bringing the right data to the people who need it, our platforms empower our partners to develop lifesaving drugs, forecast supply chain disruptions, locate missing children, and more.


The Role
 
The Connectivity team builds products that connect our most critical institutions to their most critical data. Our products securely integrate databases, enterprise applications, cloud storage, web services, and streaming systems, enabling customers to bring data into Foundry and write back to their operational systems. We build applications, frameworks, and infrastructure for connectivity across Foundry: high scale data processing pipelines, user-written code, AI agents, or connecting directly from the Ontology.

You’ll work across the stack, owning and building out features across our UI, backend services, and compute platforms. You’ll iterate closely with experienced engineers, FDEs, and other teams to scope and build out new Connectivity products and integrations, as well as building toolkits to support those integrations: APIs, SDKs, authentication flows, security frameworks, and changes to core products across the platform. The work is highly technical, collaborative, dynamic, and follows customer signal closely.

This role is expected to be about 75% backend and 25% frontend.
 

Core Responsibilities
 
We're hiring high agency engineers who are passionate about solving real-world problems. If you’re motivated to enable outcomes with connectivity, here are some examples of the types of work you’d get to do:
Build SDKs and integrations that allow customers and internal product teams to write code to connect to external systemsLaunch features to enable entirely new paradigms of data connectionDive deep into Foundry security and the bleeding edge of securing connected AI agents and pipelines in sensitive environmentsIdentify, diagnose, and remediate performance and correctness issues for high scale connectivity workflowsWork with infrastructure teams to expose powerful networking functionality to usersCraft elegant workflows to enable customers to maximally leverage their data systemsScale nascent connectivity products from first use to billionsLearn and build across a large suite of repos, services, and domains

Technologies We Use
Java and PythonOpen-source technologies like Cassandra, Kubernetes, Envoy, GraphQL, and ReactProtocols such as TCP, UDP, TLS, HTTPGradle for builds and GitHub for collaborationShared job orchestration, streaming, serverless execution, and compute deployment platforms
You do not need prior experience with these technologies. We expect you to learn them here.

lists.content:
• Curiosity about connectivity in cloud systems, from networking to productization to security and authentication
  • An ownership mindset and a high bar for usability, security, and correctness, including responsibility for how software behaves in production.
  • Comfort following problems across languages, APIs, services, networks, and execution environments
  • Eagerness to learn, ask questions, and incorporate feedback

• Currently pursuing or recently completed a Bachelor's, Master's, or PhD in Computer Science, Mathematics, Software Engineering, Physics, or a similar field, or equivalent practical experience
  • Proficiency in at least one language such as Java, Python, TypeScript, or Go
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills
  • Coursework, projects, or practical experience in one or more of computer networks, distributed systems, databases, cloud computing, or software architecture.
  • Must be planning on graduating in 2028. This should be your final internship before graduating.

description_raw:
SentiLink | https://www.sentilink.com/ | Engineering & Data Science | REMOTE, HYBRID, and ONSITE (UNITED STATES ONLY) | Full Time
Primarily hiring in the U.S. for more senior level roles. We’re hiring across Engineering (Primarily Backend/Data Platform) and Data Science / ML roles. Hiring at Manager/Director level as well as Senior IC levels. We’re language-agnostic and hire for fundamentals. Across the team you’ll see: • Python, Go, Rust, Scala • PostgreSQL, Snowflake • Kafka, Redis • Terraform, Kubernetes • ML: XGBoost, PyTorch, Feature stores, real-time scoring pipelines If you love solving complex distributed systems challenges, building customer-facing ML products, or working on detection systems that must be both high-precision and low-latency, you’ll fit right in. Apply for roles here: https://jobs.ashbyhq.com/sentilink?utm_source=hacker_news At SentiLink, we stop identity fraud at scale. We analyze millions of applications while keeping real users moving fast. We’ve seen tremendous traction and are growing extremely quickly. Our real-time APIs have helped verify hundreds of millions of identities, starting with financial services and rapidly expanding into new markets. SentiLink is backed by world-class investors including Craft Ventures, Andreessen Horowitz, NYCA, and Max Levchin. We’re a small, high-impact team solving one of the most interesting and adversarial problems in fintech: how do you build systems that reliably determine whether a real human is on the other side of a financial transaction?

description_raw: Subimage (YC W25) | Founding Engineer | San Francisco, CA | ONSITE (5 days/week) | Full-time | $170K–$230K + 0.5%–1.0% equity | https://subimage.io Hihi, I'm Alex, co-founder and CEO. Subimage maps infrastructure the way an attacker does so security teams at scale-ups and enterprises can find and fix problems. We're built on Cartography ( https://cartography.dev ), the open source infra mapping tool we helped create at Lyft and donated to the CNCF. It runs at over 70 companies, including 7 in the Fortune 100. We're a tiny seed-stage team and our customers are companies your parents have heard of. We have more demand than we can build for, which is why this post exists. This is a chance to get in on the ground floor of something big (or to find out quickly that it won't work; just being upfront about it). Some of the problems you'd be working on: - Vulnerability triage with real context: is the asset internet-facing, through which services, is the vulnerable function actually reachable in code, are there compensating controls, and what sensitive data does it reach once exploited, across how many hops. - Proving that the security fixes our agent proposes won't break anything. - A near-real-time, self-updating map of an environment so you can see an attack as it happens, plus "time travel" in the graph so you can replay it afterward. - Teaching an agent to answer questions about a large graph quickly, with only the context it needs and without making mistakes. - Determining who owns a given resource from messy signals like tags, actions, logs, and files. Stack: Cartography for ingestion, Neo4j for the graph, Python/FastAPI backend, Svelte frontend with a homegrown WebGL graph renderer, an MCP server that exposes all of it to agents, Terraform for IaC. Who we're looking for: 3+ years at high-growth companies, strong distributed systems and cloud experience, a real sense of ownership, first-principles thinking, and a willingness to implement gnarly business logic (elegantly, ideally) if it makes a jaded security engineer's life easier. Process: technical screen, call with the founders, a paid day working with the team, then offer. Health/vision/dental, 401k match, gym, team lunches, unlimited PTO. description_raw: A World-Changing Company Palantir builds the world’s leading software for data-driven decisions and operations. By bringing the right data to the people who need it, our platforms empower our partners to develop lifesaving drugs, forecast supply chain disruptions, locate missing children, and more. The Role The Connectivity team builds the software that connects Palantir’s platform to customer systems. Our connectors integrate databases, enterprise applications, cloud storage, web services, and streaming systems, enabling customers to bring data into Foundry and write back to their operational systems. From large datasets to real-time events and user-driven interactions, these connections underpin the applications and AI workflows customers build with Foundry and AIP. You’ll build and maintain Foundry’s first-class connector suite and the shared infrastructure behind it. You’ll work across the stack, taking ownership of connector implementations, developer SDKs, and the systems that build, test, distribute, and run our connectivity software. A central part of this work is evolving and scaling a large, established codebase. You’ll move integrations from bespoke infrastructure onto shared platform capabilities, design SDKs that enable other teams and customers to build integrations independently, and safely retire older implementations. You’ll also build observability and diagnostic tools that help users understand, monitor, and troubleshoot their connections. You’ll own improvements from design through production and use what you learn from operating connectors to strengthen the platform they share. Salary The estimated salary range for this position is estimated to be $135,000 - $200,000/year. Total compensation for this position may also include Restricted Stock units, sign-on bonus and other potential future incentives. Further note that total compensation for this position will be determined by each individual’s relevant qualifications, work experience, skills, and other factors. This estimate excludes the value of any potential sign-on bonus; the value of any benefits offered; and the potential future value of any long-term incentives. Life at Palantir We want every Palantirian to achieve their best outcomes, that’s why we celebrate individuals’ strengths, skills, and interests, from your first interview to your longterm growth, rather than rely on traditional career ladders. Paying attention to the needs of our community enables us to optimize our opportunities to grow and helps ensure many pathways to success at Palantir. Promoting health and well-being across all areas of Palantirians’ lives is just one of the ways we’re investing in our community. Learn more at Life at Palantir and note that our offerings may vary by region. In keeping consistent with Palantir’s values and culture, we believe employees are “better together” and in-person work affords the opportunity for more creative outcomes. Therefore, we encourage employees to work from our offices to foster connectivity and innovation. Many teams do offer hybrid options (WFH a day or two a week), allowing our employees to strike the right trade-off for their personal productivity. Based on business need, there are a few roles that allow for “Remote” work on an exceptional basis. If you are applying for one of these roles, you must work from the city and or country in which you are employed. If the posting is specified as Onsite, you are required to work from an office. If you want to empower the world's most important institutions, you belong here. Palantir values excellence regardless of background. We are committed to making the application and hiring process accessible to everyone and will provide a reasonable accommodation for those living with a disability. If you need an accommodation for the application or hiring process , please reach out and let us know how we can help. Please note that you will never be asked to submit a payment or share financial information to participate in our interview process. If you suspect that you've been contacted by a scammer, we recommend you cease all communication with the individual and consider reporting them to the relevant authorities, such as the US FBI Internet Crime Complaint Center (IC3) .

A World-Changing Company
 
Palantir builds the world’s leading software for data-driven decisions and operations. By bringing the right data to the people who need it, our platforms empower our partners to develop lifesaving drugs, forecast supply chain disruptions, locate missing children, and more.
 
The Role
 
The Connectivity team builds the software that connects Palantir’s platform to customer systems. Our connectors integrate databases, enterprise applications, cloud storage, web services, and streaming systems, enabling customers to bring data into Foundry and write back to their operational systems. From large datasets to real-time events and user-driven interactions, these connections underpin the applications and AI workflows customers build with Foundry and AIP.
 
You’ll build and maintain Foundry’s first-class connector suite and the shared infrastructure behind it. You’ll work across the stack, taking ownership of connector implementations, developer SDKs, and the systems that build, test, distribute, and run our connectivity software.
 
A central part of this work is evolving and scaling a large, established codebase. You’ll move integrations from bespoke infrastructure onto shared platform capabilities, design SDKs that enable other teams and customers to build integrations independently, and safely retire older implementations. You’ll also build observability and diagnostic tools that help users understand, monitor, and troubleshoot their connections. You’ll own improvements from design through production and use what you learn from operating connectors to strengthen the platform they share.

lists.content:
• Java and Python for connectors, backend services, and developer SDKs
  • Open-source technologies like Kafka, Kubernetes, Flink, Debezium, Iceberg
  • Industry-standard build tooling, including Gradle and GitHub
  • Shared job orchestration, streaming, serverless execution, and compute deployment platforms

• Build and maintain Foundry’s first-class connectors, improving performance and extending support for imports, exports, change data capture, interactive queries, and writeback as external systems and customer needs evolve.
  • Improve the infrastructure that builds, tests, packages, and distributes connectors and shared libraries, including tooling across our connector monorepo.
  • Design and maintain connectivity SDKs for internal teams and end users, with clear APIs, documentation, testing utilities, and development workflows that make integrations easy to author and maintain.
  • Collaborate with product teams to integrate connector execution with job orchestration, streaming, and serverless platforms.
  • Lead incremental migrations onto shared infrastructure, manage compatibility, and retire older implementations while preserving the workflows customers depend on.
  • Develop reusable security frameworks and tooling that make secure connectivity a consistent part of connector development and execution.
  • Debug production issues and performance problems across the stack, turning recurring support problems into durable fixes, automated tests, and better observability.
  • Establish shared testing frameworks, compatibility checks, and release practices that keep a large connector portfolio reliable and maintainable.
  • Help prepare and maintain Palantir connectivity software for open-source use, including its APIs, packaging, documentation, and contributor experience.

• An ownership mindset and a high bar for correctness, security, and automated testing, including responsibility for how software behaves in production.
  • Pride in building and maintaining integrations over time, including the detailed work required to keep them reliable as upstream systems change.
  • Engineering judgment that balances delivering new capabilities with simplifying existing systems and reducing operational burden.
  • Empathy for developers and end users, reflected in usable SDKs, clear configuration, actionable errors, and useful diagnostics.
  • Curiosity about unfamiliar systems and persistence in debugging problems across languages, APIs, services, networks, and execution environments.

• 4+ years of professional software engineering experience developing external system connectors, with depth in areas such as developing batch and streaming data ingestion systems, third-party integration development, or monorepo and asset distribution frameworks. Operating on top of these technologies alone does not qualify.
  • Deep expertise in Gradle, including developing custom plugins, managing multi-project builds, and optimizing build performance.
  • Demonstrated ability to diagnose complex reliability and performance problems and improve systems through measured, incremental changes.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills and the ability to work effectively across teams, incorporate feedback, and hold a high bar for quality.

lists.content:
• Build, maintain, and improve datasets and pipelines supporting Recruiting
  • Integrate data from systems such as Lever, Workday, Foundry, and other recruiting systems
  • Develop reporting datasets and dashboards for recruiting performance, candidate pipelines, recruiting programs, and operational audits
  • Evaluate existing data integrations for opportunities to reduce latency and implement necessary changes

A World-Changing Company
 
Palantir builds the world’s leading software for data-driven decisions and operations. By bringing the right data to the people who need it, our platforms empower our partners to develop lifesaving drugs, forecast supply chain disruptions, locate missing children, and more.

The Role

As a Platform Engineer on Palantir's Identity Platform team, you will design, build, and operate secure-by-design identity infrastructure and tooling. You will make identity governance and access management easier and more secure to implement for Palantirians and customers worldwide. As part of Palantir's best-in-class Information Security organization, you will research, implement, and scale innovative solutions that help Palantir stay ahead of a dynamic threat landscape.

You will help the team build the next-generation identity platform that treats agents and workload identities as first-class principals: the access graph that makes entitlements legible, the policy engine that makes authorization enforceable and auditable, and the token-issuance layer that keeps access short-lived, scoped, and least-privilege by default. Your work will shape the arc of these components from design to production.

You will join the high-performing Identity Platform team, engineers who are passionate about delivering identity outcomes at scale that reduce risk and friction. The team builds and operates the identity platforms that serve both corporate and production (customer-facing) infrastructure, and the paved-road tooling and secure baselines that teams across Palantir deploy on. Your goal will be to make the secure path the easy path. Your work will directly strengthen the identity substrate beneath Palantir's most critical deployments, from a globally distributed workforce to regulated and air-gapped environments.

lists.content:
• Develop automation and tooling for corporate and customer-facing identity platforms
  • Build, secure, and manage geo-redundant containerized services (EKS and ECS) in AWS and Azure
  • Scale the implementation of Single Sign-On (SSO) integrations across multiple Entra ID tenants using infrastructure-as-code frameworks
  • Build tooling to standardize and scale operational workflows across AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud Platform (GCP)
  • Extend the identity platform to non-human identities, treating workloads and AI agents as first-class principals with scoped, short-lived credentials
  • Build the governance layer: an access graph that makes entitlements legible and a policy engine that makes authorization decisions enforceable and auditable
  • Design token-issuance and federation flows that make least-privilege, ephemeral access the default
  • Research and drive adoption of emerging authentication and session security standards (such as device-bound session credentials and continuous access evaluation) in collaboration with Security Engineers
  • Pressure-test designs and partner with Identity Security Engineers to threat model implementations before they ship
  • Partner with Security Compliance Engineers to build services that reduce the cost and complexity of compliance enforcement

• Technical proficiency in identity protocols (SAML, OIDC, OAuth 2.0, LDAP, Kerberos, FIDO2, WebAuthn)
  • Experience managing identities and governance workflows on platforms such as Entra ID, Keycloak, AWS Cognito, or Okta
  • Experience with policy engines and authorization-as-code, and with relationship-based access modeling or entitlement graph design
  • Experience with token issuance and federation, including OAuth 2.0 token exchange, short-lived credentials, and workload identity federation
  • Non-human identity experience: workload and machine identity (service-to-service authentication, mTLS, workload attestation), plus interest in agentic identity (agents as principals, delegation and on-behalf-of flows, and attribution across a delegation chain)

• 3+ years of experience in Site Reliability Engineering (SRE), DevOps, software engineering, or an equivalent discipline, with a strong passion for security
  • Experience deploying and operating containerized services (EKS, ECS, or similar) in AWS, Azure, or Google Cloud
  • Experience building and operating production services or APIs, not only automation scripts
  • Expert-level proficiency in a language such as Go (preferred), Python, or TypeScript
  • Experience with infrastructure-as-code (Terraform, Helm, CloudFormation, or similar)
  • An active TS/SCI security clearance, or eligibility and willingness to obtain one

description_raw: A World-Changing Company Palantir builds the world’s leading software for data-driven decisions and operations. By bringing the right data to the people who need it, our platforms empower our partners to develop lifesaving drugs, forecast supply chain disruptions, locate missing children, and more. The Role The Connectivity team builds the software that connects Palantir’s platform to customer systems. Our connectors integrate databases, enterprise applications, cloud storage, web services, and streaming systems, enabling customers to bring data into Foundry and write back to their operational systems. From large datasets to real-time events and user-driven interactions, these connections underpin the applications and AI workflows customers build with Foundry and AIP. You’ll build and maintain Foundry’s first-class connector suite and the shared infrastructure behind it. You’ll work across the stack, taking ownership of connector implementations, developer SDKs, and the systems that build, test, distribute, and run our connectivity software. A central part of this work is evolving and scaling a large, established codebase. You’ll move integrations from bespoke infrastructure onto shared platform capabilities, design SDKs that enable other teams and customers to build integrations independently, and safely retire older implementations. You’ll also build observability and diagnostic tools that help users understand, monitor, and troubleshoot their connections. You’ll own improvements from design through production and use what you learn from operating connectors to strengthen the platform they share. Salary The estimated salary range for this position is estimated to be $135,000 - $200,000/year. Total compensation for this position may also include Restricted Stock units, sign-on bonus and other potential future incentives. Further note that total compensation for this position will be determined by each individual’s relevant qualifications, work experience, skills, and other factors. This estimate excludes the value of any potential sign-on bonus; the value of any benefits offered; and the potential future value of any long-term incentives. Life at Palantir We want every Palantirian to achieve their best outcomes, that’s why we celebrate individuals’ strengths, skills, and interests, from your first interview to your longterm growth, rather than rely on traditional career ladders. Paying attention to the needs of our community enables us to optimize our opportunities to grow and helps ensure many pathways to success at Palantir. Promoting health and well-being across all areas of Palantirians’ lives is just one of the ways we’re investing in our community. Learn more at Life at Palantir and note that our offerings may vary by region. In keeping consistent with Palantir’s values and culture, we believe employees are “better together” and in-person work affords the opportunity for more creative outcomes. Therefore, we encourage employees to work from our offices to foster connectivity and innovation. Many teams do offer hybrid options (WFH a day or two a week), allowing our employees to strike the right trade-off for their personal productivity. Based on business need, there are a few roles that allow for “Remote” work on an exceptional basis. If you are applying for one of these roles, you must work from the city and or country in which you are employed. If the posting is specified as Onsite, you are required to work from an office. If you want to empower the world's most important institutions, you belong here. Palantir values excellence regardless of background. We are committed to making the application and hiring process accessible to everyone and will provide a reasonable accommodation for those living with a disability. If you need an accommodation for the application or hiring process , please reach out and let us know how we can help. Please note that you will never be asked to submit a payment or share financial information to participate in our interview process. If you suspect that you've been contacted by a scammer, we recommend you cease all communication with the individual and consider reporting them to the relevant authorities, such as the US FBI Internet Crime Complaint Center (IC3) .

lists.content:
• Java and Python for connectors, backend services, and developer SDKs
  • Open-source technologies like Kafka, Kubernetes, Flink, Debezium, Iceberg
  • Industry-standard build tooling, including Gradle and GitHub
  • Shared job orchestration, streaming, serverless execution, and compute deployment platforms

• Build and maintain Foundry’s first-class connectors, improving performance and extending support for imports, exports, change data capture, interactive queries, and writeback as external systems and customer needs evolve.
  • Improve the infrastructure that builds, tests, packages, and distributes connectors and shared libraries, including tooling across our connector monorepo.
  • Design and maintain connectivity SDKs for internal teams and end users, with clear APIs, documentation, testing utilities, and development workflows that make integrations easy to author and maintain.
  • Collaborate with product teams to integrate connector execution with job orchestration, streaming, and serverless platforms.
  • Lead incremental migrations onto shared infrastructure, manage compatibility, and retire older implementations while preserving the workflows customers depend on.
  • Develop reusable security frameworks and tooling that make secure connectivity a consistent part of connector development and execution.
  • Debug production issues and performance problems across the stack, turning recurring support problems into durable fixes, automated tests, and better observability.
  • Establish shared testing frameworks, compatibility checks, and release practices that keep a large connector portfolio reliable and maintainable.
  • Help prepare and maintain Palantir connectivity software for open-source use, including its APIs, packaging, documentation, and contributor experience.

• An ownership mindset and a high bar for correctness, security, and automated testing, including responsibility for how software behaves in production.
  • Pride in building and maintaining integrations over time, including the detailed work required to keep them reliable as upstream systems change.
  • Engineering judgment that balances delivering new capabilities with simplifying existing systems and reducing operational burden.
  • Empathy for developers and end users, reflected in usable SDKs, clear configuration, actionable errors, and useful diagnostics.
  • Curiosity about unfamiliar systems and persistence in debugging problems across languages, APIs, services, networks, and execution environments.

• 4+ years of professional software engineering experience developing external system connectors, with depth in areas such as developing batch and streaming data ingestion systems, third-party integration development, or monorepo and asset distribution frameworks. Operating on top of these technologies alone does not qualify.
  • Deep expertise in Gradle, including developing custom plugins, managing multi-project builds, and optimizing build performance.
  • Demonstrated ability to diagnose complex reliability and performance problems and improve systems through measured, incremental changes.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills and the ability to work effectively across teams, incorporate feedback, and hold a high bar for quality.

A World-Changing Company
 
Palantir builds the world’s leading software for data-driven decisions and operations. By bringing the right data to the people who need it, our platforms empower our partners to develop lifesaving drugs, forecast supply chain disruptions, locate missing children, and more.

The Role

As a Platform Engineer on Palantir's Identity Platform team, you will design, build, and operate secure-by-design identity infrastructure and tooling. You will make identity governance and access management easier and more secure to implement for Palantirians and customers worldwide. As part of Palantir's best-in-class Information Security organization, you will research, implement, and scale innovative solutions that help Palantir stay ahead of a dynamic threat landscape.

You will help the team build the next-generation identity platform that treats agents and workload identities as first-class principals: the access graph that makes entitlements legible, the policy engine that makes authorization enforceable and auditable, and the token-issuance layer that keeps access short-lived, scoped, and least-privilege by default. Your work will shape the arc of these components from design to production.

You will join the high-performing Identity Platform team, engineers who are passionate about delivering identity outcomes at scale that reduce risk and friction. The team builds and operates the identity platforms that serve both corporate and production (customer-facing) infrastructure, and the paved-road tooling and secure baselines that teams across Palantir deploy on. Your goal will be to make the secure path the easy path. Your work will directly strengthen the identity substrate beneath Palantir's most critical deployments, from a globally distributed workforce to regulated and air-gapped environments.

lists.content:
• Develop automation and tooling for corporate and customer-facing identity platforms
  • Build, secure, and manage geo-redundant containerized services (EKS and ECS) in AWS and Azure
  • Scale the implementation of Single Sign-On (SSO) integrations across multiple Entra ID tenants using infrastructure-as-code frameworks
  • Build tooling to standardize and scale operational workflows across AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud Platform (GCP)
  • Extend the identity platform to non-human identities, treating workloads and AI agents as first-class principals with scoped, short-lived credentials
  • Build the governance layer: an access graph that makes entitlements legible and a policy engine that makes authorization decisions enforceable and auditable
  • Design token-issuance and federation flows that make least-privilege, ephemeral access the default
  • Research and drive adoption of emerging authentication and session security standards (such as device-bound session credentials and continuous access evaluation) in collaboration with Security Engineers
  • Pressure-test designs and partner with Identity Security Engineers to threat model implementations before they ship
  • Partner with Security Compliance Engineers to build services that reduce the cost and complexity of compliance enforcement

• Technical proficiency in identity protocols (SAML, OIDC, OAuth 2.0, LDAP, Kerberos, FIDO2, WebAuthn)
  • Experience managing identities and governance workflows on platforms such as Entra ID, Keycloak, AWS Cognito, or Okta
  • Experience with policy engines and authorization-as-code, and with relationship-based access modeling or entitlement graph design
  • Experience with token issuance and federation, including OAuth 2.0 token exchange, short-lived credentials, and workload identity federation
  • Non-human identity experience: workload and machine identity (service-to-service authentication, mTLS, workload attestation), plus interest in agentic identity (agents as principals, delegation and on-behalf-of flows, and attribution across a delegation chain)

• 3+ years of experience in Site Reliability Engineering (SRE), DevOps, software engineering, or an equivalent discipline, with a strong passion for security
  • Experience deploying and operating containerized services (EKS, ECS, or similar) in AWS, Azure, or Google Cloud
  • Experience building and operating production services or APIs, not only automation scripts
  • Expert-level proficiency in a language such as Go (preferred), Python, or TypeScript
  • Experience with infrastructure-as-code (Terraform, Helm, CloudFormation, or similar)
  • An active TS/SCI security clearance, or eligibility and willingness to obtain one

description_raw: A World-Changing Company Palantir builds the world’s leading software for data-driven decisions and operations. By bringing the right data to the people who need it, our platforms empower our partners to develop lifesaving drugs, forecast supply chain disruptions, locate missing children, and more. The Role The Connectivity team builds the software that connects Palantir’s platform to customer systems. Our connectors integrate databases, enterprise applications, cloud storage, web services, and streaming systems, enabling customers to bring data into Foundry and write back to their operational systems. From large datasets to real-time events and user-driven interactions, these connections underpin the applications and AI workflows customers build with Foundry and AIP. You’ll build and maintain Foundry’s first-class connector suite and the shared infrastructure behind it. You’ll work across the stack, taking ownership of connector implementations, developer SDKs, and the systems that build, test, distribute, and run our connectivity software. A central part of this work is evolving and scaling a large, established codebase. You’ll move integrations from bespoke infrastructure onto shared platform capabilities, design SDKs that enable other teams and customers to build integrations independently, and safely retire older implementations. You’ll also build observability and diagnostic tools that help users understand, monitor, and troubleshoot their connections. You’ll own improvements from design through production and use what you learn from operating connectors to strengthen the platform they share.
