lists.content:
• Java and Python for connectors, backend services, and developer SDKs
  • Open-source technologies like Kafka, Kubernetes, Flink, Debezium, Iceberg
  • Industry-standard build tooling, including Gradle and GitHub
  • Shared job orchestration, streaming, serverless execution, and compute deployment platforms

• Build and maintain Foundry’s first-class connectors, improving performance and extending support for imports, exports, change data capture, interactive queries, and writeback as external systems and customer needs evolve.
  • Improve the infrastructure that builds, tests, packages, and distributes connectors and shared libraries, including tooling across our connector monorepo.
  • Design and maintain connectivity SDKs for internal teams and end users, with clear APIs, documentation, testing utilities, and development workflows that make integrations easy to author and maintain.
  • Collaborate with product teams to integrate connector execution with job orchestration, streaming, and serverless platforms.
  • Lead incremental migrations onto shared infrastructure, manage compatibility, and retire older implementations while preserving the workflows customers depend on.
  • Develop reusable security frameworks and tooling that make secure connectivity a consistent part of connector development and execution.
  • Debug production issues and performance problems across the stack, turning recurring support problems into durable fixes, automated tests, and better observability.
  • Establish shared testing frameworks, compatibility checks, and release practices that keep a large connector portfolio reliable and maintainable.
  • Help prepare and maintain Palantir connectivity software for open-source use, including its APIs, packaging, documentation, and contributor experience.

• An ownership mindset and a high bar for correctness, security, and automated testing, including responsibility for how software behaves in production.
  • Pride in building and maintaining integrations over time, including the detailed work required to keep them reliable as upstream systems change.
  • Engineering judgment that balances delivering new capabilities with simplifying existing systems and reducing operational burden.
  • Empathy for developers and end users, reflected in usable SDKs, clear configuration, actionable errors, and useful diagnostics.
  • Curiosity about unfamiliar systems and persistence in debugging problems across languages, APIs, services, networks, and execution environments.

• 4+ years of professional software engineering experience developing external system connectors, with depth in areas such as developing batch and streaming data ingestion systems, third-party integration development, or monorepo and asset distribution frameworks. Operating on top of these technologies alone does not qualify.
  • Deep expertise in Gradle, including developing custom plugins, managing multi-project builds, and optimizing build performance.
  • Demonstrated ability to diagnose complex reliability and performance problems and improve systems through measured, incremental changes.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills and the ability to work effectively across teams, incorporate feedback, and hold a high bar for quality.

A World-Changing Company
 
Palantir builds the world’s leading software for data-driven decisions and operations. By bringing the right data to the people who need it, our platforms empower our partners to develop lifesaving drugs, forecast supply chain disruptions, locate missing children, and more.

The Role

As a Platform Engineer on Palantir's Identity Platform team, you will design, build, and operate secure-by-design identity infrastructure and tooling. You will make identity governance and access management easier and more secure to implement for Palantirians and customers worldwide. As part of Palantir's best-in-class Information Security organization, you will research, implement, and scale innovative solutions that help Palantir stay ahead of a dynamic threat landscape.

You will help the team build the next-generation identity platform that treats agents and workload identities as first-class principals: the access graph that makes entitlements legible, the policy engine that makes authorization enforceable and auditable, and the token-issuance layer that keeps access short-lived, scoped, and least-privilege by default. Your work will shape the arc of these components from design to production.

You will join the high-performing Identity Platform team, engineers who are passionate about delivering identity outcomes at scale that reduce risk and friction. The team builds and operates the identity platforms that serve both corporate and production (customer-facing) infrastructure, and the paved-road tooling and secure baselines that teams across Palantir deploy on. Your goal will be to make the secure path the easy path. Your work will directly strengthen the identity substrate beneath Palantir's most critical deployments, from a globally distributed workforce to regulated and air-gapped environments.

lists.content:
• Develop automation and tooling for corporate and customer-facing identity platforms
  • Build, secure, and manage geo-redundant containerized services (EKS and ECS) in AWS and Azure
  • Scale the implementation of Single Sign-On (SSO) integrations across multiple Entra ID tenants using infrastructure-as-code frameworks
  • Build tooling to standardize and scale operational workflows across AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud Platform (GCP)
  • Extend the identity platform to non-human identities, treating workloads and AI agents as first-class principals with scoped, short-lived credentials
  • Build the governance layer: an access graph that makes entitlements legible and a policy engine that makes authorization decisions enforceable and auditable
  • Design token-issuance and federation flows that make least-privilege, ephemeral access the default
  • Research and drive adoption of emerging authentication and session security standards (such as device-bound session credentials and continuous access evaluation) in collaboration with Security Engineers
  • Pressure-test designs and partner with Identity Security Engineers to threat model implementations before they ship
  • Partner with Security Compliance Engineers to build services that reduce the cost and complexity of compliance enforcement

• Technical proficiency in identity protocols (SAML, OIDC, OAuth 2.0, LDAP, Kerberos, FIDO2, WebAuthn)
  • Experience managing identities and governance workflows on platforms such as Entra ID, Keycloak, AWS Cognito, or Okta
  • Experience with policy engines and authorization-as-code, and with relationship-based access modeling or entitlement graph design
  • Experience with token issuance and federation, including OAuth 2.0 token exchange, short-lived credentials, and workload identity federation
  • Non-human identity experience: workload and machine identity (service-to-service authentication, mTLS, workload attestation), plus interest in agentic identity (agents as principals, delegation and on-behalf-of flows, and attribution across a delegation chain)

• 3+ years of experience in Site Reliability Engineering (SRE), DevOps, software engineering, or an equivalent discipline, with a strong passion for security
  • Experience deploying and operating containerized services (EKS, ECS, or similar) in AWS, Azure, or Google Cloud
  • Experience building and operating production services or APIs, not only automation scripts
  • Expert-level proficiency in a language such as Go (preferred), Python, or TypeScript
  • Experience with infrastructure-as-code (Terraform, Helm, CloudFormation, or similar)
  • An active TS/SCI security clearance, or eligibility and willingness to obtain one

description_raw: A World-Changing Company Palantir builds the world’s leading software for data-driven decisions and operations. By bringing the right data to the people who need it, our platforms empower our partners to develop lifesaving drugs, forecast supply chain disruptions, locate missing children, and more. The Role The Connectivity team builds the software that connects Palantir’s platform to customer systems. Our connectors integrate databases, enterprise applications, cloud storage, web services, and streaming systems, enabling customers to bring data into Foundry and write back to their operational systems. From large datasets to real-time events and user-driven interactions, these connections underpin the applications and AI workflows customers build with Foundry and AIP. You’ll build and maintain Foundry’s first-class connector suite and the shared infrastructure behind it. You’ll work across the stack, taking ownership of connector implementations, developer SDKs, and the systems that build, test, distribute, and run our connectivity software. A central part of this work is evolving and scaling a large, established codebase. You’ll move integrations from bespoke infrastructure onto shared platform capabilities, design SDKs that enable other teams and customers to build integrations independently, and safely retire older implementations. You’ll also build observability and diagnostic tools that help users understand, monitor, and troubleshoot their connections. You’ll own improvements from design through production and use what you learn from operating connectors to strengthen the platform they share. Salary The estimated salary range for this position is estimated to be $135,000 - $200,000/year. Total compensation for this position may also include Restricted Stock units, sign-on bonus and other potential future incentives. Further note that total compensation for this position will be determined by each individual’s relevant qualifications, work experience, skills, and other factors. This estimate excludes the value of any potential sign-on bonus; the value of any benefits offered; and the potential future value of any long-term incentives. lists.content:
• Java and Python for connectors, backend services, and developer SDKs
  • Open-source technologies like Kafka, Kubernetes, Flink, Debezium, Iceberg
  • Industry-standard build tooling, including Gradle and GitHub
  • Shared job orchestration, streaming, serverless execution, and compute deployment platforms

• Build and maintain Foundry’s first-class connectors, improving performance and extending support for imports, exports, change data capture, interactive queries, and writeback as external systems and customer needs evolve.
  • Improve the infrastructure that builds, tests, packages, and distributes connectors and shared libraries, including tooling across our connector monorepo.
  • Design and maintain connectivity SDKs for internal teams and end users, with clear APIs, documentation, testing utilities, and development workflows that make integrations easy to author and maintain.
  • Collaborate with product teams to integrate connector execution with job orchestration, streaming, and serverless platforms.
  • Lead incremental migrations onto shared infrastructure, manage compatibility, and retire older implementations while preserving the workflows customers depend on.
  • Develop reusable security frameworks and tooling that make secure connectivity a consistent part of connector development and execution.
  • Debug production issues and performance problems across the stack, turning recurring support problems into durable fixes, automated tests, and better observability.
  • Establish shared testing frameworks, compatibility checks, and release practices that keep a large connector portfolio reliable and maintainable.
  • Help prepare and maintain Palantir connectivity software for open-source use, including its APIs, packaging, documentation, and contributor experience.

• An ownership mindset and a high bar for correctness, security, and automated testing, including responsibility for how software behaves in production.
  • Pride in building and maintaining integrations over time, including the detailed work required to keep them reliable as upstream systems change.
  • Engineering judgment that balances delivering new capabilities with simplifying existing systems and reducing operational burden.
  • Empathy for developers and end users, reflected in usable SDKs, clear configuration, actionable errors, and useful diagnostics.
  • Curiosity about unfamiliar systems and persistence in debugging problems across languages, APIs, services, networks, and execution environments.

• 4+ years of professional software engineering experience developing external system connectors, with depth in areas such as developing batch and streaming data ingestion systems, third-party integration development, or monorepo and asset distribution frameworks. Operating on top of these technologies alone does not qualify.
  • Deep expertise in Gradle, including developing custom plugins, managing multi-project builds, and optimizing build performance.
  • Demonstrated ability to diagnose complex reliability and performance problems and improve systems through measured, incremental changes.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills and the ability to work effectively across teams, incorporate feedback, and hold a high bar for quality.

lists.content:

A World-Changing Company
 
Palantir builds the world’s leading software for data-driven decisions and operations. By bringing the right data to the people who need it, our platforms empower our partners to develop lifesaving drugs, forecast supply chain disruptions, locate missing children, and more.

The Role

As a Platform Engineer on Palantir's Identity Platform team, you will design, build, and operate secure-by-design identity infrastructure and tooling. You will make identity governance and access management easier and more secure to implement for Palantirians and customers worldwide. As part of Palantir's best-in-class Information Security organization, you will research, implement, and scale innovative solutions that help Palantir stay ahead of a dynamic threat landscape.

You will help the team build the next-generation identity platform that treats agents and workload identities as first-class principals: the access graph that makes entitlements legible, the policy engine that makes authorization enforceable and auditable, and the token-issuance layer that keeps access short-lived, scoped, and least-privilege by default. Your work will shape the arc of these components from design to production.

You will join the high-performing Identity Platform team, engineers who are passionate about delivering identity outcomes at scale that reduce risk and friction. The team builds and operates the identity platforms that serve both corporate and production (customer-facing) infrastructure, and the paved-road tooling and secure baselines that teams across Palantir deploy on. Your goal will be to make the secure path the easy path. Your work will directly strengthen the identity substrate beneath Palantir's most critical deployments, from a globally distributed workforce to regulated and air-gapped environments.

lists.content:
• Develop automation and tooling for corporate and customer-facing identity platforms
  • Build, secure, and manage geo-redundant containerized services (EKS and ECS) in AWS and Azure
  • Scale the implementation of Single Sign-On (SSO) integrations across multiple Entra ID tenants using infrastructure-as-code frameworks
  • Build tooling to standardize and scale operational workflows across AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud Platform (GCP)
  • Extend the identity platform to non-human identities, treating workloads and AI agents as first-class principals with scoped, short-lived credentials
  • Build the governance layer: an access graph that makes entitlements legible and a policy engine that makes authorization decisions enforceable and auditable
  • Design token-issuance and federation flows that make least-privilege, ephemeral access the default
  • Research and drive adoption of emerging authentication and session security standards (such as device-bound session credentials and continuous access evaluation) in collaboration with Security Engineers
  • Pressure-test designs and partner with Identity Security Engineers to threat model implementations before they ship
  • Partner with Security Compliance Engineers to build services that reduce the cost and complexity of compliance enforcement

• Technical proficiency in identity protocols (SAML, OIDC, OAuth 2.0, LDAP, Kerberos, FIDO2, WebAuthn)
  • Experience managing identities and governance workflows on platforms such as Entra ID, Keycloak, AWS Cognito, or Okta
  • Experience with policy engines and authorization-as-code, and with relationship-based access modeling or entitlement graph design
  • Experience with token issuance and federation, including OAuth 2.0 token exchange, short-lived credentials, and workload identity federation
  • Non-human identity experience: workload and machine identity (service-to-service authentication, mTLS, workload attestation), plus interest in agentic identity (agents as principals, delegation and on-behalf-of flows, and attribution across a delegation chain)

• 3+ years of experience in Site Reliability Engineering (SRE), DevOps, software engineering, or an equivalent discipline, with a strong passion for security
  • Experience deploying and operating containerized services (EKS, ECS, or similar) in AWS, Azure, or Google Cloud
  • Experience building and operating production services or APIs, not only automation scripts
  • Expert-level proficiency in a language such as Go (preferred), Python, or TypeScript
  • Experience with infrastructure-as-code (Terraform, Helm, CloudFormation, or similar)
  • An active TS/SCI security clearance, or eligibility and willingness to obtain one

description_raw: A World-Changing Company Palantir builds the world’s leading software for data-driven decisions and operations. By bringing the right data to the people who need it, our platforms empower our partners to develop lifesaving drugs, forecast supply chain disruptions, locate missing children, and more. The Role The Connectivity team builds the software that connects Palantir’s platform to customer systems. Our connectors integrate databases, enterprise applications, cloud storage, web services, and streaming systems, enabling customers to bring data into Foundry and write back to their operational systems. From large datasets to real-time events and user-driven interactions, these connections underpin the applications and AI workflows customers build with Foundry and AIP. You’ll build and maintain Foundry’s first-class connector suite and the shared infrastructure behind it. You’ll work across the stack, taking ownership of connector implementations, developer SDKs, and the systems that build, test, distribute, and run our connectivity software. A central part of this work is evolving and scaling a large, established codebase. You’ll move integrations from bespoke infrastructure onto shared platform capabilities, design SDKs that enable other teams and customers to build integrations independently, and safely retire older implementations. You’ll also build observability and diagnostic tools that help users understand, monitor, and troubleshoot their connections. You’ll own improvements from design through production and use what you learn from operating connectors to strengthen the platform they share. Salary The estimated salary range for this position is estimated to be $135,000 - $200,000/year. Total compensation for this position may also include Restricted Stock units, sign-on bonus and other potential future incentives. Further note that total compensation for this position will be determined by each individual’s relevant qualifications, work experience, skills, and other factors. This estimate excludes the value of any potential sign-on bonus; the value of any benefits offered; and the potential future value of any long-term incentives. Life at Palantir We want every Palantirian to achieve their best outcomes, that’s why we celebrate individuals’ strengths, skills, and interests, from your first interview to your longterm growth, rather than rely on traditional career ladders. Paying attention to the needs of our community enables us to optimize our opportunities to grow and helps ensure many pathways to success at Palantir. Promoting health and well-being across all areas of Palantirians’ lives is just one of the ways we’re investing in our community. In keeping consistent with Palantir’s values and culture, we believe employees are “better together” and in-person work affords the opportunity for more creative outcomes. Therefore, we encourage employees to work from our offices to foster connectivity and innovation. Many teams do offer hybrid options (WFH a day or two a week), allowing our employees to strike the right trade-off for their personal productivity. Based on business need, there are a few roles that allow for “Remote” work on an exceptional basis. If you are applying for one of these roles, you must work from the city and or country in which you are employed. If the posting is specified as Onsite, you are required to work from an office. If you want to empower the world's most important institutions, you belong here. Palantir values excellence regardless of background. We are committed to making the application and hiring process accessible to everyone and will provide a reasonable accommodation for those living with a disability. If you need an accommodation for the application or hiring process , please reach out and let us know how we can help. Please note that you will never be asked to submit a payment or share financial information to participate in our interview process. If you suspect that you've been contacted by a scammer, we recommend you cease all communication with the individual and consider reporting them to the relevant authorities, such as the US FBI Internet Crime Complaint Center (IC3) .

lists.content:
• Java and Python for connectors, backend services, and developer SDKs
  • Open-source technologies like Kafka, Kubernetes, Flink, Debezium, Iceberg
  • Industry-standard build tooling, including Gradle and GitHub
  • Shared job orchestration, streaming, serverless execution, and compute deployment platforms

• Build and maintain Foundry’s first-class connectors, improving performance and extending support for imports, exports, change data capture, interactive queries, and writeback as external systems and customer needs evolve.
  • Improve the infrastructure that builds, tests, packages, and distributes connectors and shared libraries, including tooling across our connector monorepo.
  • Design and maintain connectivity SDKs for internal teams and end users, with clear APIs, documentation, testing utilities, and development workflows that make integrations easy to author and maintain.
  • Collaborate with product teams to integrate connector execution with job orchestration, streaming, and serverless platforms.
  • Lead incremental migrations onto shared infrastructure, manage compatibility, and retire older implementations while preserving the workflows customers depend on.
  • Develop reusable security frameworks and tooling that make secure connectivity a consistent part of connector development and execution.
  • Debug production issues and performance problems across the stack, turning recurring support problems into durable fixes, automated tests, and better observability.
  • Establish shared testing frameworks, compatibility checks, and release practices that keep a large connector portfolio reliable and maintainable.
  • Help prepare and maintain Palantir connectivity software for open-source use, including its APIs, packaging, documentation, and contributor experience.

• An ownership mindset and a high bar for correctness, security, and automated testing, including responsibility for how software behaves in production.
  • Pride in building and maintaining integrations over time, including the detailed work required to keep them reliable as upstream systems change.
  • Engineering judgment that balances delivering new capabilities with simplifying existing systems and reducing operational burden.
  • Empathy for developers and end users, reflected in usable SDKs, clear configuration, actionable errors, and useful diagnostics.
  • Curiosity about unfamiliar systems and persistence in debugging problems across languages, APIs, services, networks, and execution environments.

• 4+ years of professional software engineering experience developing external system connectors, with depth in areas such as developing batch and streaming data ingestion systems, third-party integration development, or monorepo and asset distribution frameworks. Operating on top of these technologies alone does not qualify.
  • Deep expertise in Gradle, including developing custom plugins, managing multi-project builds, and optimizing build performance.
  • Demonstrated ability to diagnose complex reliability and performance problems and improve systems through measured, incremental changes.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills and the ability to work effectively across teams, incorporate feedback, and hold a high bar for quality.

The Role
 
Software Engineers at Palantir build software at scale to transform how organizations use data. Our Software Engineers are involved throughout the product lifecycle, from idea generation, design, prototyping, and production delivery. You will collaborate closely with technical and non-technical teammates to understand our customers' problems and build products that solve them. We encourage movement across teams to share context, skills, and experience, so you'll learn about many different technologies and aspects of each product. Engineers work autonomously and make decisions independently, within a community that will support and challenge you as you grow and develop, becoming a strong technical contributor and engineering leader.

Our infrastructure teams are responsible for the lowest layers of our software stack, often focused on database technologies, distributed systems, large scale data systems, security, and application infrastructure. As a Software Engineer on infrastructure working on our Foundry platform, you'll contribute high-quality code to underpin Palantir Foundry and Gotham with performant, secure, and scalable building blocks, enabling products deployed to the most important institutions in the public and private sector. You'll build the foundational capabilities that power our products used by research scientists, aerospace engineers, intelligence analysts, and economic forecasters, in countries around the world.
 
We’re hiring engineers who are passionate about solving real-world problems and empowering both developers and end-users to work optimally. If you’re motivated to develop reliable, performant, and scalable systems, and to design robust APIs and primitives, this role offers the opportunity to make a significant impact on our products and the people who use them.
 
Frontline
 
Foundry Software Engineers may be offered the opportunity to Frontline, an exclusive program unlike any other. This unique, short-term assignment involves being embedded with customers, allowing you to work directly with users and gain firsthand insight into how our products are used and the challenges our customers face. Some of our most successful products were built on the factory floor, addressing real-world problems for the world's most important institutions. No two days are alike, as each day is diverse and impactful. By witnessing how customers engage with Foundry and experiencing these pain points firsthand, you’ll gain unique insights that feed directly back into our development process, helping to refine and enhance our products.

lists.content:
• Building a performant search and indexing ecosystem for complex granularly permissioned data
  • Contributing to open-source data processing libraries, integrating the latest innovations to achieve performance gains
  • Building the distributed systems that power large scale compute workloads, orchestrating and efficiently scheduling hundreds of thousands of containers every hour
  • Designing architecture and opinionated APIs to keep application developers on the happy path
  • Tracing and performance observability in high scale distributed microservice architectures
  • Building reliant, performant, and scalable systems for storage, auth, or asset serving to enable other product teams to build robust applications without deep domain expertise in the underlying systems
  • Automating the deployment, management, and operations of complex distributed systems like Cassandra, Elasticsearch, Kafka, and more across different environments

• Different backend languages, including Java, Rust, and Go
  • Open-source technologies like Cassandra, ElasticSearch, Spark, Kafka, Kubernetes, Flink
  • Industry-standard build tooling, including Gradle and GitHub

• Demonstrated ability to collaborate and empathize with a variety of individuals. Able to iterate with users and non-technical stakeholders and understand how technical decisions impact them.
  • Ability to learn new technology and concepts, even without in-depth experience. Experience developing and managing highly-available distributed systems is beneficial, but not required.
  • Bias towards quality and thoughtful about edge cases (“anything that can go wrong will go wrong”); writes code that is defensive against all possibilities.
  • Builds solutions and APIs with users in mind while maintaining a high engineering bar. Seeks to centralize and abstract complexity away from our users in order to expose simple, powerful APIs for consumers.
  • Active US Security clearance, or eligibility and willingness to obtain a US Security clearance is beneficial, but not necessary.

• Engineering background in Computer Science, Mathematics, Software Engineering, Physics or similar field.
  • Strong coding skills with demonstrated proficiency in programming languages, such as Java, C++, Python, Rust, or similar languages.
  • Familiarity with storage and data processing systems, cloud infrastructure, and other technical tools.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills and ability to iterate quickly with teammates, incorporating feedback and holding a high bar for quality.

lists.content:
• Building a performant search and indexing ecosystem for complex granularly permissioned data
  • Contributing to open-source data processing libraries, integrating the latest innovations to achieve performance gains
  • Building the distributed systems that power large scale compute workloads, orchestrating and efficiently scheduling hundreds of thousands of containers every hour
  • Designing architecture and opinionated APIs to keep application developers on the happy path
  • Tracing and performance observability in high scale distributed microservice architectures
  • Building reliant, performant, and scalable systems for storage, auth, or asset serving to enable other product teams to build robust applications without deep domain expertise in the underlying systems
  • Automating the deployment, management, and operations of complex distributed systems like Cassandra, Elasticsearch, Kafka, and more across different environments

• Different backend languages, including Java, Rust, and Go
  • Open-source technologies like Cassandra, ElasticSearch, Spark, Kafka, Kubernetes, Flink
  • Industry-standard build tooling, including Gradle and GitHub

• Demonstrated ability to collaborate and empathize with a variety of individuals. Able to iterate with users and non-technical stakeholders and understand how technical decisions impact them.
  • Ability to learn new technology and concepts, even without in-depth experience. Experience developing and managing highly-available distributed systems is beneficial, but not required.
  • Bias towards quality and thoughtful about edge cases (“anything that can go wrong will go wrong”); writes code that is defensive against all possibilities.
  • Builds solutions and APIs with users in mind while maintaining a high engineering bar. Seeks to centralize and abstract complexity away from our users in order to expose simple, powerful APIs for consumers.
  • Active US Security clearance, or eligibility and willingness to obtain a US Security clearance is beneficial, but not necessary.

• Engineering background in Computer Science, Mathematics, Software Engineering, Physics or similar field.
  • Strong coding skills with demonstrated proficiency in programming languages, such as Java, C++, Python, Rust, or similar languages.
  • Familiarity with storage and data processing systems, cloud infrastructure, and other technical tools.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills and ability to iterate quickly with teammates, incorporating feedback and holding a high bar for quality.

lists.content:
• Build, maintain, and improve datasets and pipelines supporting Recruiting
  • Integrate data from systems such as Lever, Workday, Foundry, and other recruiting systems
  • Develop reporting datasets and dashboards for recruiting performance, candidate pipelines, recruiting programs, and operational audits
  • Evaluate existing data integrations for opportunities to reduce latency and implement necessary changes
  • Partner with central Data and platform teams on warehouse connections, schema changes, API behavior, and source-system migrations
  • Support integrations between recruiting systems and internal tools including writeback of data updates
  • Design data access and reporting solutions that respect confidentiality, role-based permissions, and regional or organizational access boundaries
  • Create clear documentation for sensitive workflows and ensure that operational users understand the limitations of the data

  • Familiarity with workflow automation, writeback processes, and event-driven integrations

• Degree in Data Science, Finance, Math, Engineering, Computer Science, Economics, Business or other quantitative fields
  • 1+ years of experience in a data analytical role
  • Expertise in Python and data manipulation to answer complex questions. Experience with pySpark, pandas, or polars is a plus.
  • Strong SQL skills and experience working with relational or structured data.
  • Proficiency with BI tools, SQL, and the organization and analysis of data
  • Fluency in TypeScript, or another general-purpose programming language
  • Ability to create reusable data models, testing frameworks, and data quality checks

raw_payload.descriptionPlain:
A World-Changing Company
 
Palantir builds the world’s leading software for data-driven decisions and operations. By bringing the right data to the people who need it, our platforms empower our partners to develop lifesaving drugs, forecast supply chain disruptions, locate missing children, and more.


The Role
As a Platform Engineer on Palantir's Identity Platform team, you will design, build, and operate secure-by-design identity infrastructure and tooling. You will make identity governance and access management easier and more secure to implement for Palantirians and customers worldwide. As part of Palantir's best-in-class Information Security organization, you will research, implement, and scale innovative solutions that help Palantir stay ahead of a dynamic threat landscape.

You will help the team build the next-generation identity platform that treats agents and workload identities as first-class principals: the access graph that makes entitlements legible, the policy engine that makes authorization enforceable and auditable, and the token-issuance layer that keeps access short-lived, scoped, and least-privilege by default. Your work will shape the arc of these components from design to production.

You will join the high-performing Identity Platform team, engineers who are passionate about delivering identity outcomes at scale that reduce risk and friction. The team builds and operates the identity platforms that serve both corporate and production (customer-facing) infrastructure, and the paved-road tooling and secure baselines that teams across Palantir deploy on. Your goal will be to make the secure path the easy path. Your work will directly strengthen the identity substrate beneath Palantir's most critical deployments, from a globally distributed workforce to regulated and air-gapped environments.

lists.content:
• Develop automation and tooling for corporate and customer-facing identity platforms
  • Build, secure, and manage geo-redundant containerized services (EKS and ECS) in AWS and Azure
  • Scale the implementation of Single Sign-On (SSO) integrations across multiple Entra ID tenants using infrastructure-as-code frameworks
  • Build tooling to standardize and scale operational workflows across AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud Platform (GCP)
  • Extend the identity platform to non-human identities, treating workloads and AI agents as first-class principals with scoped, short-lived credentials
  • Build the governance layer: an access graph that makes entitlements legible and a policy engine that makes authorization decisions enforceable and auditable
  • Design token-issuance and federation flows that make least-privilege, ephemeral access the default
  • Research and drive adoption of emerging authentication and session security standards (such as device-bound session credentials and continuous access evaluation) in collaboration with Security Engineers
  • Pressure-test designs and partner with Identity Security Engineers to threat model implementations before they ship
  • Partner with Security Compliance Engineers to build services that reduce the cost and complexity of compliance enforcement

• Technical proficiency in identity protocols (SAML, OIDC, OAuth 2.0, LDAP, Kerberos, FIDO2, WebAuthn)
  • Experience managing identities and governance workflows on platforms such as Entra ID, Keycloak, AWS Cognito, or Okta
  • Experience with policy engines and authorization-as-code, and with relationship-based access modeling or entitlement graph design
  • Experience with token issuance and federation, including OAuth 2.0 token exchange, short-lived credentials, and workload identity federation
  • Non-human identity experience: workload and machine identity (service-to-service authentication, mTLS, workload attestation), plus interest in agentic identity (agents as principals, delegation and on-behalf-of flows, and attribution across a delegation chain)

• 3+ years of experience in Site Reliability Engineering (SRE), DevOps, software engineering, or an equivalent discipline, with a strong passion for security
  • Experience deploying and operating containerized services (EKS, ECS, or similar) in AWS, Azure, or Google Cloud
  • Experience building and operating production services or APIs, not only automation scripts
  • Expert-level proficiency in a language such as Go (preferred), Python, or TypeScript
  • Experience with infrastructure-as-code (Terraform, Helm, CloudFormation, or similar)
  • An active TS/SCI security clearance, or eligibility and willingness to obtain one

As a Platform Engineer on Palantir's Identity Platform team, you will design, build, and operate secure-by-design identity infrastructure and tooling. You will make identity governance and access management easier and more secure to implement for Palantirians and customers worldwide. As part of Palantir's best-in-class Information Security organization, you will research, implement, and scale innovative solutions that help Palantir stay ahead of a dynamic threat landscape.

You will help the team build the next-generation identity platform that treats agents and workload identities as first-class principals: the access graph that makes entitlements legible, the policy engine that makes authorization enforceable and auditable, and the token-issuance layer that keeps access short-lived, scoped, and least-privilege by default. Your work will shape the arc of these components from design to production.

You will join the high-performing Identity Platform team, engineers who are passionate about delivering identity outcomes at scale that reduce risk and friction. The team builds and operates the identity platforms that serve both corporate and production (customer-facing) infrastructure, and the paved-road tooling and secure baselines that teams across Palantir deploy on. Your goal will be to make the secure path the easy path. Your work will directly strengthen the identity substrate beneath Palantir's most critical deployments, from a globally distributed workforce to regulated and air-gapped environments.

lists.content:
• Develop automation and tooling for corporate and customer-facing identity platforms
  • Build, secure, and manage geo-redundant containerized services (EKS and ECS) in AWS and Azure
  • Scale the implementation of Single Sign-On (SSO) integrations across multiple Entra ID tenants using infrastructure-as-code frameworks
  • Build tooling to standardize and scale operational workflows across AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud Platform (GCP)
  • Extend the identity platform to non-human identities, treating workloads and AI agents as first-class principals with scoped, short-lived credentials
  • Build the governance layer: an access graph that makes entitlements legible and a policy engine that makes authorization decisions enforceable and auditable
  • Design token-issuance and federation flows that make least-privilege, ephemeral access the default
  • Research and drive adoption of emerging authentication and session security standards (such as device-bound session credentials and continuous access evaluation) in collaboration with Security Engineers
  • Pressure-test designs and partner with Identity Security Engineers to threat model implementations before they ship
  • Partner with Security Compliance Engineers to build services that reduce the cost and complexity of compliance enforcement

• Technical proficiency in identity protocols (SAML, OIDC, OAuth 2.0, LDAP, Kerberos, FIDO2, WebAuthn)
  • Experience managing identities and governance workflows on platforms such as Entra ID, Keycloak, AWS Cognito, or Okta
  • Experience with policy engines and authorization-as-code, and with relationship-based access modeling or entitlement graph design
  • Experience with token issuance and federation, including OAuth 2.0 token exchange, short-lived credentials, and workload identity federation
  • Non-human identity experience: workload and machine identity (service-to-service authentication, mTLS, workload attestation), plus interest in agentic identity (agents as principals, delegation and on-behalf-of flows, and attribution across a delegation chain)

• 3+ years of experience in Site Reliability Engineering (SRE), DevOps, software engineering, or an equivalent discipline, with a strong passion for security
  • Experience deploying and operating containerized services (EKS, ECS, or similar) in AWS, Azure, or Google Cloud
  • Experience building and operating production services or APIs, not only automation scripts
  • Expert-level proficiency in a language such as Go (preferred), Python, or TypeScript
  • Experience with infrastructure-as-code (Terraform, Helm, CloudFormation, or similar)
  • An active TS/SCI security clearance, or eligibility and willingness to obtain one

Our Software Engineers are involved throughout the product lifecycle, from idea generation, design, prototyping, and production delivery. You will collaborate closely with technical and non-technical teammates to understand our customers' problems and build products that solve them. We encourage movement across teams to share context, skills, and experience, so you'll learn about many different technologies and aspects of each product. Engineers work autonomously and make decisions independently, within a community that will support and challenge you as you grow and develop, becoming a strong technical contributor and engineering leader. Our Product Development organization is made up of small teams of Software Engineers. Each team focuses on a specific aspect of a product. Our infrastructure teams are responsible for the lowest layers of our software stack, often focused on database technologies, distributed systems, large scale data systems, security, and application infrastructure. As a Software Engineer on infrastructure working on our Foundry platform, you'll contribute high-quality code to underpin Palantir Foundry and Gotham with performant, secure, and scalable building blocks, enabling products deployed to the most important institutions in the public and private sector. You'll build the foundational capabilities that power our products used by research scientists, aerospace engineers, intelligence analysts, and economic forecasters, in countries around the world. We’re hiring engineers who are passionate about solving real-world problems and empowering both developers and end-users to work optimally. If you’re motivated to develop reliable, performant, and scalable systems, and to design robust APIs and primitives, this role offers the opportunity to make a significant impact on our products and the people who use them. Frontline Foundry Software Engineers may be offered the opportunity to Frontline, an exclusive program unlike any other. This unique, short-term assignment involves being embedded with customers, allowing you to work directly with users and gain firsthand insight into how our products are used and the challenges our customers face. Unlike traditional engineering roles, Frontline immerses you in complex, ambiguous problems, empowering you to deliver impactful solutions across some of the world’s most important industries and institutions. Some of our most successful products were built on the factory floor, addressing real-world problems for the world's most important institutions. These products were developed by some of our most successful product engineers, who began their careers in roles aligned with Frontline responsibilities, gaining a deep understanding of both our technology and our customers. raw_payload.descriptionPlain:
A World-Changing Company
 
Palantir builds the world’s leading software for data-driven decisions and operations. By bringing the right data to the people who need it, our platforms empower our partners to develop lifesaving drugs, forecast supply chain disruptions, locate missing children, and more.


The Role
 
Software Engineers at Palantir build software at scale to transform how organizations use data. Our Software Engineers are involved throughout the product lifecycle, from idea generation, design, prototyping, and production delivery. You will collaborate closely with technical and non-technical teammates to understand our customers' problems and build products that solve them. We encourage movement across teams to share context, skills, and experience, so you'll learn about many different technologies and aspects of each product. Engineers work autonomously and make decisions independently, within a community that will support and challenge you as you grow and develop, becoming a strong technical contributor and engineering leader.

Our Product Development organization is made up of small teams of Software Engineers. Each team focuses on a specific aspect of a product. Our infrastructure teams are responsible for the lowest layers of our software stack, often focused on database technologies, distributed systems, large scale data systems, security, and application infrastructure. As a Software Engineer on infrastructure working on our Foundry platform, you'll contribute high-quality code to underpin Palantir Foundry and Gotham with performant, secure, and scalable building blocks, enabling products deployed to the most important institutions in the public and private sector. You'll build the foundational capabilities that power our products used by research scientists, aerospace engineers, intelligence analysts, and economic forecasters, in countries around the world.

We’re hiring engineers who are passionate about solving real-world problems and empowering both developers and end-users to work optimally. If you’re motivated to develop reliable, performant, and scalable systems, and to design robust APIs and primitives, this role offers the opportunity to make a significant impact on our products and the people who use them.

Frontline
 
Foundry Software Engineers may be offered the opportunity to Frontline, an exclusive program unlike any other. This unique, short-term assignment involves being embedded with customers, allowing you to work directly with users and gain firsthand insight into how our products are used and the challenges our customers face. Unlike traditional engineering roles, Frontline immerses you in complex, ambiguous problems, empowering you to deliver impactful solutions across some of the world’s most important industries and institutions.

Some of our most successful products were built on the factory floor, addressing real-world problems for the world's most important institutions. These products were developed by some of our most successful product engineers, who began their careers in roles aligned with Frontline responsibilities, gaining a deep understanding of both our technology and our customers.

Frontliners operate across a broad spectrum of responsibilities, much like a startup CTO. They work in small teams to own the end-to-end execution of high-stakes projects. This spectrum ranges from discussing architecture and building custom web apps to conducting workshops with users and strategizing with customer executives. No two days are alike, as each day is diverse and impactful. By witnessing how customers engage with Foundry and experiencing these pain points firsthand, you’ll gain unique insights that feed directly back into our development process, helping to refine and enhance our products.

lists.content:
• Building a performant search and indexing ecosystem for complex granularly permissioned data
  • Contributing to open-source data processing libraries, integrating the latest innovations to achieve performance gains
  • Building the distributed systems that power large scale compute workloads, orchestrating and efficiently scheduling hundreds of thousands of containers every hour
  • Designing architecture and opinionated APIs to keep application developers on the happy path
  • Tracing and performance observability in high scale distributed microservice architectures
  • Building reliant, performant, and scalable systems for storage, auth, or asset serving to enable other product teams to build robust applications without deep domain expertise in the underlying systems
  • Automating the deployment, management, and operations of complex distributed systems like Cassandra, Elasticsearch, Kafka, and more across different environments

• Different backend languages, including Java, Rust, and Go
  • Open-source technologies like Cassandra, ElasticSearch, Spark, Kafka, Kubernetes, Flink
  • Industry-standard build tooling, including Gradle and GitHub

• Demonstrated ability to collaborate and empathize with a variety of individuals. Able to iterate with users and non-technical stakeholders and understand how technical decisions impact them.
  • Ability to learn new technology and concepts, even without in-depth experience. Experience developing and managing highly-available distributed systems is beneficial, but not required.
  • Bias towards quality and thoughtful about edge cases (“anything that can go wrong will go wrong”); writes code that is defensive against all possibilities.
  • Leading solutions and APIs with users in mind while maintaining a high engineering bar. Seeks to centralize and abstract complexity away from our users in order to expose simple, powerful APIs for consumers.
  • Active US Security clearance, or eligibility and willingness to obtain a US Security clearance is beneficial, but not necessary.

• 6+ years of experience designing, building, and operating scalable and reliable infrastructure systems in a production environment
  • Engineering background in Computer Science, Mathematics, Software Engineering, Physics or similar field.
  • Strong coding skills with demonstrated proficiency in programming languages, such as Java, C++, Python, Rust, or similar languages.
  • Familiarity with storage and data processing systems, cloud infrastructure, and other technical tools.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills and ability to iterate quickly with teammates, incorporating feedback and holding a high bar for quality.

Both are front-facing development roles for someone who loves both tech and tackling real business problems. We love people with prior experience in multiple industries. SentiLink | https://www.sentilink.com/ | Engineering & Data Science | REMOTE, HYBRID, and ONSITE (UNITED STATES ONLY) | Full Time
Primarily hiring in the U.S. for more senior level roles. We’re hiring across Engineering (Primarily Backend/Data Platform) and Data Science / ML roles. Hiring at Manager/Director level as well as Senior IC levels. We’re language-agnostic and hire for fundamentals. Across the team you’ll see: • Python, Go, Rust, Scala • PostgreSQL, Snowflake • Kafka, Redis • Terraform, Kubernetes • ML: XGBoost, PyTorch, Feature stores, real-time scoring pipelines If you love solving complex distributed systems challenges, building customer-facing ML products, or working on detection systems that must be both high-precision and low-latency, you’ll fit right in. We’re a small, high-impact team solving one of the most interesting and adversarial problems in fintech: how do you build systems that reliably determine whether a real human is on the other side of a financial transaction?

description_raw: Blockrotate| Senior Systems / Rust Engineer | Remote (US/EU timezones preferred) | Full-time | $130k - $170k + Equity Blockrotate ( https://blockrotate.com ) builds low-latency copy-trading and execution infrastructure for Polymarket and prediction markets. Copy trading on prediction markets has strange market microstructure. Unlike deep perp DEXes (Binance, Hyperliquid), Polymarket orderbooks are bounded, often thin, and subject to severe adverse selection. When a high-volume leader buys, the book moves immediately. If followers lag by a few hundred milliseconds, or if a platform taxes every order with a 50bps fee, follower alpha drops to zero. Most existing tools in this space either hit users with high per-trade taker fees or ask them to export and paste their master private key into a database. We took a different approach: isolated per-bot deposit wallets (non-custodial via EIP-1967/1271 proxies) and co-located autonomous Rust workers running delta-sync loops directly against the Polymarket CLOB. Stack: - Backend: Rust, Tokio, Axum, Protobuf over WebSockets, SQLite (WAL mode) - Trading Engine: Custom Polymarket CLOB & Data API clients, EIP-712 signing, dynamic slippage ladders, momentum filters, circuit breakers - Frontend: Next.js 16, React 19, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS What you’d actually work on: - Squeezing latency out of the execution hot path (delta position calculation, order placement, nonce handling, fill verification). - Building better execution protection: momentum filters to dodge toxic order flow, fill stabilization windows, and handling thin book liquidity without moving the market against yourself. - Scaling worker orchestration: our C2 server talks Protobuf to distributed bot workers with monotonic sequence IDs and autonomous reconnect failover. As bot volume scales, we need to keep state reconciliation bulletproof. - Investigating and exploiting prediction market quirks (rebate structures, orderbook snapshotting, MEV/relayer bottlenecks). What we look for: - Strong async Rust experience (Tokio, concurrency, practical memory management). - Experience dealing with websockets, exchange orderbooks, or trading infrastructure shoot an email to jobs@blockrotate.com and tell us why you would be a good fit for us.

description_raw: Lumen Labs | Robotics/Hardware Engineer, Simulation Engineer | San Francisco, CA | ONSITE | Full-time | $150k–200k + equity | https://lumenresearch.co Howdy! Lumen Labs is building the cognitive layer for physical AI. Nearly every major robotics effort today teaches machines by showing them thousands of hours of human teleoperation. We think that paradigm has a ceiling, and we’re working on nature-inspired architectures for unstructured environments (construction sites, mining, pipelines, battlefield). Pre-seed, backed by top VC funds and operators from robotics/AI companies. Today we run wheeled navigation, we’re dipping our toes into drones, and we’re eyeing weirder platforms like home inspection. We’re a small team hiring two engineers who will work closely with each other and with our model engineer: ROBOTICS / HARDWARE ENGINEER: Own the hardware and infrastructure that keeps our research platforms running: the ROS2 (Humble) stack across onboard and offboard compute, sensor integration and calibration (LiDAR, depth, IMU, encoders), the safety pipeline during autonomous runs, and getting trained policies onto real hardware. Will be hands-on with real mobile robots (UART, encoders, PWM, IMU, LiDAR), strong Python + embedded, comfortable reading code you didn’t write, and can debug hardware and firmware at the same time. Full posting: https://desert-bearskin-26d.notion.site/Robotics-Engineer-Ro... SIMULATION ENGINEER: Own “the gauntlet,” our test library for putting new architectures through their paces: a Gymnasium-style interface on both sides (environment and model) so anything built to spec is compatible with everything else. Mostly MuJoCo and Gazebo today, moving toward Isaac Sim, and some other more bespoke sims. You will be building task simulators for training and testing and keeping them running (GPS-denied drone nav, construction sites, boat cleaning, forklifts, abstract control), including physics, honest sensor models, digital twins of our real platforms, domain randomization, and the sim compute.  Dungeon Master. If you have built or substantially rebuilt a simulator of some kind (robotics/RL is closest, but a physics-based game, scientific sim, or flight sim mod counts) this would be a good role for you. Comfortable with the Gymnasium/dm_control way of thinking, can pick up GPU-vectorized sim (MJX, Isaac Lab, JAX) quickly, and test-driven. Full posting: https://desert-bearskin-26d.notion.site/Simulation-Engineer-... Email hi@lumenresearch.co, mention HN and which role, and tell us about a project you’ve built. If you can link to a trained policy running on real hardware (robotics) or a simulator you built or fixed and something you trained inside it (sim), you go to the top of the pile.

description_raw: Paramark | Software Engineer (L4) | San Francisco HYBRID (3 days/wk) or REMOTE (US) | Full-time | $199K–$249K + equity Paramark helps Marketing teams optimize spend across all of their channels and programs. There are proven scientific ways to do this, but they are poorly understood and practiced by only a tiny fraction of teams. Our product ingests data from all of our customers' marketing channels and uses it to train open-source ML models for both measurement and experimentation.  This makes it possible for any marketer to use these methods. In this domain, it's hard to figure out what to build, and it's even harder to be both accurate and simple. You'll be joining a small team -- we have four product engineers. That means owning systems end to end and having real influence over what gets built. Your typical project will start with a high level goal, and you will figure out the rest. Founded 2023, ~16 people, $8M from Greylock, cash-flow positive. Reasonable working hours: when the Mercury News covered the return of 996 culture, we were the counterexample. "We don't think early stage startup life requires 18-hour days, or even 12-hour days." https://www.mercurynews.com/2025/08/25/silicon-valley-startu... . 4 weeks PTO plus federal holidays, medical/dental/vision (100% of employee premiums, 50% for family). Looking for 8+ years, full-stack. Some exposure to statistics, experimentation, or A/B testing helps. Stack: TypeScript, React, Python, Postgres.  Google Cloud, Kubernetes, FastAPI, taskiq. Process: intro call; technical phone screen; one-day onsite in SF (travel covered for remote candidates) In-person: https://paramark.com/careers/software-engineer-l4 Remote: https://paramark.com/careers/software-engineer-l4-remote I'm the CTO and I read every application myself. description_raw: Subimage (YC W25) | Founding Engineer | San Francisco, CA | ONSITE (5 days/week) | Full-time | $170K–$230K + 0.5%–1.0% equity | https://subimage.io Hihi, I'm Alex, co-founder and CEO. Subimage maps infrastructure the way an attacker does so security teams at scale-ups and enterprises can find and fix problems. We're built on Cartography ( https://cartography.dev ), the open source infra mapping tool we helped create at Lyft and donated to the CNCF. It runs at over 70 companies, including 7 in the Fortune 100. We're a tiny seed-stage team and our customers are companies your parents have heard of. We have more demand than we can build for, which is why this post exists. This is a chance to get in on the ground floor of something big (or to find out quickly that it won't work; just being upfront about it). Some of the problems you'd be working on: - Vulnerability triage with real context: is the asset internet-facing, through which services, is the vulnerable function actually reachable in code, are there compensating controls, and what sensitive data does it reach once exploited, across how many hops. - Proving that the security fixes our agent proposes won't break anything. - A near-real-time, self-updating map of an environment so you can see an attack as it happens, plus "time travel" in the graph so you can replay it afterward. - Teaching an agent to answer questions about a large graph quickly, with only the context it needs and without making mistakes. - Determining who owns a given resource from messy signals like tags, actions, logs, and files. Stack: Cartography for ingestion, Neo4j for the graph, Python/FastAPI backend, Svelte frontend with a homegrown WebGL graph renderer, an MCP server that exposes all of it to agents, Terraform for IaC. Who we're looking for: 3+ years at high-growth companies, strong distributed systems and cloud experience, a real sense of ownership, first-principles thinking, and a willingness to implement gnarly business logic (elegantly, ideally) if it makes a jaded security engineer's life easier. Kubernetes and security knowledge are nice to have, not required. You're in the Bay Area and want to be in the office five days a week. Process: technical screen, call with the founders, a paid day working with the team, then offer. Health/vision/dental, 401k match, gym, team lunches, unlimited PTO. Apply here and mention HN: https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/subimage/jobs/NCTFgKK-...

description_raw: Stratirus (a Tennetech company) | AI Developer + Linux Admin (junior to mid) | REMOTE (US only, Central Time hours) | US work authorization required, no sponsorship | Full-time or part-time, contract or hire | $65k to $100k | No agencies Our optional take-home is a broken Ubuntu server: a service that won't stay up, a nightly report that hasn't gone out in days, and a disk that keeps filling. Fix it, write a script that heals a fresh box, and build a small read-only MCP tool so an AI agent can check on it. 60 to 90 minutes, unpaid, no LeetCode. If that sounds like fun, read on. We're a small and growing AI and Microsoft 365 consultancy in Franklin, TN. We build AI agents and automation for small and mid-sized businesses, and harden and run the systems underneath: Microsoft 365 tenants, SharePoint, and Linux boxes. We're AI-agnostic and use what fits the client, mostly Claude Code, the Microsoft 365 stack with Copilot and Copilot Studio, Gemini and Gemini Studio, and Oracle OBI. The role is about 60% agent development (MCP servers, Claude Code, Copilot Studio, Power Automate, Gemini) and 40% Ubuntu administration (systemd, Docker, patching, backups, monitoring). PeopleSoft experience is a plus. You'll work directly with clients, so explaining things clearly to a small-business owner matters as much as the code. Early-career and career-switchers welcome. We expect you to use AI every day. What we hire for is knowing when it's wrong, so one of our three application questions asks about a time it fooled you. To apply, email your resume to hiring@stratirus.com with short answers to: a time a client or boss made an unreasonable demand and how you handled it; a time an AI confidently gave you a wrong answer you followed, and how you caught it; and something you've built with AI that you still use. Work samples get strong preference. We read every application ourselves and reply to everyone, so please write your answers yourself. Process: email application, a 45-minute video call where you walk us through something you've built, then a conversation about the role. Remote within the US only, Central Time business hours. Must be legally authorized to work in the US without visa sponsorship, now or in the future. No recruiters or agencies, please. https://github.com/Stratirus/ops-agent-challenge Questions: hiring@stratirus.com

description_raw: ArtCraft | Senior Engineers | SF (Onsite) / Atlanta (Onsite) | $150-$250k + Equity | https://getartcraft.com Those fucking rent-seeking hyperscalers took the internet away from you, and we’re going to give it back to you and to everyone. Web 1.0 was great - we had IRC, file sharing, third party chat clients. There were personal websites, forums. Flash was a format kids could use. Everything supported embedding and uploading. Websites actually had APIs and RSS. File sharing, FTP, MP3s, discs, owned media. Broadband brought our parents and grandparents online, but the shift to the non-technical majority created an opportunity to grossly oversimplify everything. Everything dumbed down into a pre-packaged product. Startups began turning their offerings into walled gardens. Platforms took precedence over protocols. APIs and access and data export went away. And then the rent-seeking began. The era of ownership ended. Corporate Memphis. Jesus Christ. We’ve rallied a massive community to build MIT/Apache-licensed alternatives to Adobe, Microsoft Office, Google Workspace, Autodesk, SolidWorks, Slack, Discord, Unreal Engine, OpenRouter, RunPod, and more. The goal is full feature parity, with code anyone can own, inspect, modify, and build on. We’re digesting second-class apps and platforms into first-class applications, libraries, and APIs with full MCP support. We’re distilling out the good parts, and we’re building the connective tissue that draws them together. 100% of the internet is going to be open source soon, and we’re going to force it open. Loudly. We have eight figures in run rate revenue, over 20M app downloads and growing. Our community is the best part, and it’s energetic like a wildfire. Everyone resonates with our mission. We’re missionaries, not mercenaries. We are going to slay the incumbents by being better. Our motto is Google’s old motto - “Don't be evil (tm)”. We’re a tiny team looking for strong engineers to own major parts of the product: desktop apps, lots of completely open source backend infrastructure, agent workflows, agentic app factories. Stack: Rust, a sprinkle of TypeScript/React, egui, Tauri, MySQL/Postgres, Redis, Elasticsearch, Kubernetes. Lots and lots of Rust. We’re systems engineers by trade, but we like to vibe code Rust. Did I say Rust? Rust. Rust Rust Rust. Maybe that's a filter. You have to be self-directed and independent. If you want to open source Salesforce with half your time, do it! If you want to work on Solidworks 3D printing applications, great! Writing music apps and DAWs? Go for it! Custom Discord/Slack clients for our custom, completely open source chat API and platform? Hell yeah. Our organization is flat, and we're going to go after everybody and everything. Everything you build here will be open source. We have no private repos. We can reclaim the internet. That’s our mission. Want to know more about us? Look up “Adobe ArtCraft” on YouTube / TikTok / your platform of choice. If this resonates with you, email hn@storyteller.ai with your Github, a little about yourself and something you’ve built. Write the sentence, “don’t take my RAM, Sam!” so we know you’re one of the good guys.

description_raw: Estuary | US-Based / Remote | Full-time – https://estuary.dev/ Estuary is a VC-backed, post–Series A startup powering real-time data replication and transform — from sub-second CDC replication to terabyte-scale OLAP data flows. We’re open-source, developer-first, and focused on making data movement radically simpler across both our Platform and Applications layers. We’re hiring for: Head of Engineering — Own the engineering function end-to-end as a partner to our founder CTO: strategy, people, delivery, and operations across a compact but high-leverage team. You’ll grow the leaders already running our teams, set technical strategy jointly with the CTO, and be accountable for what engineering ships and what it costs. Senior Systems Engineer (Control & Data Plane) — Build the high-performance backbone of our platform: the orchestration, distributed state, and stream transport that keep pipelines at sub-second latency under massive throughput. You’ll work primarily in Rust on fault tolerance, consensus, and networking, and help set the bar for correctness and performance across the team. Product Manager — Own product areas end-to-end, working closely with engineering and design to shape the roadmap and deliver a great developer experience. Engage with users, translate real-world use cases into product decisions, and help define how modern data infrastructure should feel to build with. Head of Product Marketing — Lead product marketing as we bring real-time, agent-ready data pipelines to technical buyers, partnering closely with our Head of Marketing, Developer Relations, and the founders. Own positioning, messaging, launches, and competitive narrative, turning what our engineers ship into stories data teams actually care about. Solutions Engineer — Partner with sales and customers from the first technical call through production, running discovery, demos, and proofs of concept for data engineering and platform teams. You’ll design CDC, streaming, and batch pipelines on Estuary, solve real integration problems hands-on, and feed what you learn back to Product and Engineering. Customer Success Manager — Own the post-sale relationship for our data engineering and platform customers as our first CS hire. You’ll build onboarding, account health monitoring, and the expansion playbook from scratch while staying technical enough to resolve most issues yourself. Senior Compliance Engineer — Own our GDPR and PCI DSS programs while keeping our audited SOC 2 and HIPAA programs running smoothly, alongside hands-on ownership of identity, endpoint, and SaaS estate management. This is a governance-first role for someone who has run a compliance program end-to-end, not just contributed to one. What we’re looking for: People who care about building reliable, maintainable systems and processes and enjoy working with complex APIs, data flows, or customer relationships. We value curiosity, clear communication, and a willingness to learn. Bonus points for experience with CDC tools, open source contributions, or fast-paced startups. To apply: Email your resume to careers@estuary.dev

description_raw: Don't Use This Code: https://dutc.io | Training & Consulting | Full-Time (W-2) | Fully Remote (US-only) Don't Use This Code's mission statement grew out of a joke… let's look at something amazing that will change the way you think about this programming language feature or this open source library… just DON'T USE THIS CODE. I (the poster of this) made a little of a name for myself in the Python community through this very approach. See: https://pyvideo.org/speaker/james-powell.html or https://www.youtube.com/@dutctv or https://www.youtube.com/@PyDataTV/search?query=james%20powel... The core principle is: true expertise and expert knowledge is worthwhile to develop and disseminate (and this is true even if the LLM is doing a lot of the typing.) To this end, our goal is to deliver a combination of training, consulting, and hybrid coaching services to clients in the tech industry, in financial services, and at large-scale scientific research facilities. In fact, on the back of some recent successes, we are gearing up to build up a team and dramatically expand this work. Our work involves a lot of data analysis, data visualization, modelling, simulation, and experiment tooling system and infrastructure, and is currently very Python and PyData heavy. We are looking to hire both junior and senior technical leads, as well as instructors. We're just beginning to ramp up our hiring process, but provisional job reqs are available: - Senior Tech Lead: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1_uJdBJlGmin4gQ_9kxxFS7cH... - Junior Tech Lead: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1_uJdBJlGmin4gQ_9kxxFS7cH... - Instructor: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1_uJdBJlGmin4gQ_9kxxFS7cH... Given the nature of our clients, we are especially fond of hiring people with background in the sciences, including those in fields like biology or psychology, who have a strong (perhaps even self-taught) technical background. E-mail with your résumé or LinkedIn and add any thoughts you have on developing and sharing expert knowledge: jobs@dutc.io

description_raw:
MixRank (YC S11) | Software Engineers | 100% Remote (Global) | Full-Time MixRank processes petabytes of data every month through web crawling. Hundreds of customers use our data products, including Google, Amazon, Facebook, Intel, and Adobe, across industries such as finance, recruiting, sales, marketing, and security. We’re a fully remote company with a global footprint across 20+ countries. We’re growing, profitable, employee-owned, and have no dependence on outside funding. Applicants from all geographies and backgrounds are welcome. We’re looking for passionate individuals for whom programming is not just a job, but something they genuinely love to do. We’re obsessed with computers, programming, big data, databases, compilers, hardware, math, data science, and the internet. Does this sound like you? Please apply to join our team. Our codebase is friendly to new contributors. You’ll have a fully functional development environment within hours through full automation and will be pushing commits on your first day. Deployments to production happen multiple times per day and finish in under two minutes.Effectively all of our codebase is written in Python, Rust, SQL, JavaScript/TypeScript, and Nix. The core technologies you’ll need familiarity with to be productive are Python, PostgreSQL, Linux, and Git.
We operate at a larger scale than typical startups. We run two datacenters with high-performance servers we’ve built ourselves, capable of handling the volumes of data we process. We’ve implemented our own distributed file system, perform full-scale web crawls, and download and run static analysis on the entire universe of published Android APKs and iOS IPAs. Unlike a typical startup where you might spend half your time in meetings and the other half fixing Jira tickets, at MixRank you’ll challenge yourself with difficult technical problems that help you grow as an individual. We’re continuously hiring for the positions below; these aren’t singular roles that close once filled. Our philosophy is that the candidate is more important than the position. For each new member of the team, we design a custom role and responsibilities around their interests. Other companies may create a long list of specific requirements with the expectation that you’ll exactly replace someone on the team or fit a role defined by committee. MixRank is more pragmatic: we first get excited about bringing a unique individual onto the team, then figure out the best way to support their specific talents. Junior Software Engineer - Remote (Global), Full-Time We’re looking for remote junior engineers with 0–3 years of professional software experience and 5+ years of curiosity exploring computers, programming, and technical hobby projects. This is an open-ended entry role with mentorship and diverse opportunities to work across all areas of our product: databases, distributed systems, infrastructure and tooling, data analysis, machine learning, frontend/backend web development, APIs, data mining, data modeling, and more. To stand out, please highlight what makes you unique: passion for computing, curiosity and side projects, work ethic, niche research, or anything else that shows how you think and build. Ideally, you’ve already graduated. But if you still have one or more years left of school, please feel free to apply anyway. If you’re the right fit for the team, we’ll figure out a way to accommodate your schedule. Apply here: https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/mixrank/jobs/Fnwsojk-j Software Engineer - Remote (Global), Full-Time We’re hiring generalist software engineers to work on web applications, data mining, machine learning/data science, data transformation/ETL, data modeling, database scaling, infrastructure, DevOps, and more. We’ll tailor the role to the subset of areas that best match your interests. Beneficial experience includes PostgreSQL, Python, Rust, Linux, TypeScript, Nix, frontend/backend web development, and data mining. Apply here: https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/mixrank/jobs/RXQspen-s I’m Kiran, Chief of Staff at MixRank, a fully remote data startup building go-to-market intelligence. We’re US-incorporated but hire globally, and we’re bringing on new teammates to join a fast-moving team with real ownership and impact.
